options: Time for all atoms to decay|Time for half the atoms to decay|Time for one atom to decay|Time for the mass to halve once
answer: Time for half the atoms to decay
rubric: Half-life is the time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to undergo decay.

subject: Physics
stem: A machine with velocity ratio of 4 and efficiency of 80% has a mechanical advantage of _____.
rubric: MA = efficiency × VR / 100 = 80/100 × 4 = 3.2.

subject: Physics
stem: Diffraction of waves is most noticeable when the wavelength is _____ the size of the opening.
options: Much larger than|Much smaller than|Comparable to|Independent of
rubric: Diffraction is most pronounced when the wavelength of the wave is approximately equal to the size of the gap or obstacle.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following converts chemical energy to electrical energy?
options: Motor|Transformer|Battery|Generator
rubric: A battery (electrochemical cell) converts chemical energy stored in its materials into electrical energy.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is an alkene?
options: CH₄|C₂H₆|C₂H₄|C₃H₈
rubric: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a C=C double bond and general formula CₙH₂ₙ. C₂H₄ (ethene) is an alkene.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is a strong acid?
options: Ethanoic acid|Citric acid|Hydrochloric acid|Carbonic acid
rubric: HCl is a strong acid that fully dissociates in water; ethanoic and citric acids are weak acids.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In the reaction Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ iron is being _____.
options: Reduced|Oxidised|Precipitated|Neutralised
rubric: Fe²⁺ is losing an electron to form Fe³⁺ — loss of electrons is oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Hydrogen bonding occurs between molecules containing H and _____.
options: Carbon|Nitrogen oxygen or fluorine|Sulphur|Chlorine
rubric: Hydrogen bonds form when hydrogen is bonded to highly electronegative atoms — N, O, or F — creating partial charges.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, how many moles of NH₃ are produced from 1 mole of N₂?
rubric: The stoichiometric ratio shows 1 mole of N₂ reacts with 3 moles of H₂ to produce 2 moles of NH₃.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which particle determines the chemical properties of an element?
options: Neutrons|Protons|Electrons|Nucleus
rubric: The number and arrangement of electrons (especially valence electrons) determine how an element reacts chemically.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Across a period in the periodic table atomic radius _____.
options: Increases|Decreases|Stays the same|First increases then decreases
rubric: Across a period, increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer to the nucleus, so atomic radius decreases.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of CH₃COOH is _____.
options: Methanoic acid|Ethanoic acid|Propanoic acid|Butanoic acid
rubric: CH₃COOH has 2 carbon atoms and a carboxylic acid group; its IUPAC name is ethanoic acid (common name: acetic acid).

subject: Chemistry
stem: In a reversible reaction at equilibrium the _____.
options: Reaction stops|Forward and backward rates are equal|Concentrations become zero|Reactants are all used up
answer: Forward and backward rates are equal
rubric: At dynamic equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction, so concentrations remain constant.

subject: Chemistry
stem: During electrolysis of dilute H₂SO₄ which gas is produced at the cathode?
options: Oxygen|Hydrogen|Chlorine|Sulphur dioxide
rubric: At the cathode (negative electrode), H⁺ ions are discharged and hydrogen gas is produced: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which gas turns lime water milky?
options: O₂|H₂|CO₂|N₂
rubric: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) reacts with calcium hydroxide (lime water) to form calcium carbonate — a white precipitate that makes the solution milky.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The process of breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter ones using heat and a catalyst is _____.
options: Polymerisation|Cracking|Distillation|Hydrogenation
rubric: Cracking breaks down large hydrocarbon molecules (from crude oil fractions) into more useful shorter-chain molecules.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An atom that has gained electrons becomes a _____.
options: Cation|Anion|Neutral atom|Isotope
rubric: When an atom gains electrons it acquires a negative charge and becomes an anion (negatively charged ion).

subject: Chemistry
stem: What type of reaction is: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂?
options: Synthesis|Decomposition|Displacement|Neutralisation
rubric: A decomposition reaction is one in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The most electronegative element is _____.
options: Oxygen|Nitrogen|Fluorine|Chlorine
rubric: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of all elements on the Pauling scale (3.98).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Addition of H₂ to an alkene to produce an alkane is called _____.
options: Cracking|Polymerisation|Hydrogenation|Halogenation
rubric: Hydrogenation is the addition of hydrogen (H₂) across the double bond of an alkene using a catalyst (usually nickel).

subject: Chemistry
stem: A buffer solution resists changes in _____.
options: Temperature|Pressure|pH|Colour
rubric: A buffer solution maintains a relatively constant pH when small amounts of acid or base are added to it.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which type of solid has the highest melting point?
options: Ionic|Molecular|Covalent network|Metallic
rubric: Giant covalent (covalent network) solids like diamond have extremely high melting points due to strong covalent bonds throughout.

subject: Chemistry
stem: How many molecules are in 2 moles of CO₂? (Nₐ = 6.02×10²³)
rubric: Number of molecules = moles × Avogadro's number = 2 × 6.02×10²³ = 1.20×10²⁴.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Ethanol belongs to the class of organic compounds called _____.
options: Alkanes|Alcohols|Acids|Esters
rubric: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) contains the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group and belongs to the alcohol family.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Noble gases are unreactive because they have _____.
options: No protons|Full outer electron shells|No electrons|Very large nuclei
rubric: Noble gases have complete outer electron shells (octet), making them extremely stable and unreactive.

subject: Chemistry
stem: When sodium reacts with water the products are sodium hydroxide and _____.
options: Oxygen|Hydrogen|Chlorine|Carbon dioxide
rubric: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂; sodium reacts vigorously with water releasing hydrogen gas.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The electrode at which oxidation occurs in an electrochemical cell is the _____.
options: Cathode|Anode|Neutral electrode|Salt bridge
rubric: At the anode, oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs; at the cathode, reduction (gain of electrons) occurs.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which type of isomerism do CH₃CH₂OH and CH₃OCH₃ exhibit?
options: Chain isomerism|Positional isomerism|Functional group isomerism|Optical isomerism
rubric: CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol) and CH₃OCH₃ (dimethyl ether) have the same molecular formula (C₂H₆O) but different functional groups.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is the monomer of polyethylene?
options: Propene|Styrene|Ethene|Acetylene
rubric: Polyethylene (polythene) is made by polymerising ethene (CH₂=CH₂) molecules — ethene is the monomer.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An element has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. How many neutrons does it have?
rubric: Number of neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 35 - 17 = 18.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is an acid-base indicator?
options: Litmus|Fehling's solution|Benedict's reagent|Biuret reagent
rubric: Litmus is a natural acid-base indicator: red in acid, blue in alkali.

subject: Chemistry
stem: If the molar mass of NaCl is 58.5 g/mol, how many moles are in 117 g?
rubric: Moles = mass/molar mass = 117/58.5 = 2 moles.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following elements is a halogen?
options: Sodium|Chlorine|Calcium|Argon
rubric: Halogens are Group VIIA elements: F, Cl, Br, I, At. Chlorine is a halogen.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The type of bond in NaCl is _____.
options: Covalent|Metallic|Ionic|Hydrogen
rubric: NaCl is formed by the transfer of an electron from Na (metal) to Cl (non-metal), creating ionic bonds.

subject: Chemistry
stem: At constant temperature and pressure when a gas dissolves in water its solubility increases as pressure _____.
options: Decreases|Increases|Stays constant|Becomes zero
rubric: Henry's Law: the solubility of a gas in a liquid increases with increasing partial pressure of the gas above the liquid.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The ester formed from ethanol and ethanoic acid is _____.
options: Ethyl methanoate|Ethyl ethanoate|Methyl ethanoate|Methyl methanoate
rubric: Esterification: ethanol (C₂H₅OH) + ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) → ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₂H₅) + H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following reactions produces a precipitate?
options: HCl + NaOH|AgNO₃ + NaCl|H₂ + Cl₂|CO₂ + H₂O
rubric: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃. Silver chloride (AgCl) is an insoluble white precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The process of coating a cheap metal with a more precious one using electrolysis is called _____.
options: Anodising|Electroplating|Galvanising|Tempering
rubric: Electroplating deposits a thin layer of a metal (e.g. silver or gold) onto an object through electrolysis.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of _____ but different numbers of _____.
options: Neutrons; protons|Protons; neutrons|Electrons; protons|Protons; electrons
rubric: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but differ in mass number due to different numbers of neutrons.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Elements in Group IIA are called _____.
options: Alkali metals|Halogens|Noble gases|Alkaline earth metals
rubric: Group IIA elements — Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra — are called alkaline earth metals.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Fermentation of glucose produces _____.
options: Methanol and CO₂|Ethanol and CO₂|Propanol and H₂|Butanol and H₂O
rubric: Yeast ferments glucose: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. This is the basis of alcohol production.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The conjugate base of H₂O is _____.
options: OH⁻|H₃O⁺|H₂|O²⁻
rubric: According to Brønsted-Lowry theory, when H₂O donates a proton (H⁺), it becomes OH⁻ — its conjugate base.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of water are produced from 4 moles of H₂?
rubric: The ratio is 2H₂: 2H₂O (1:1), so 4 moles of H₂ produce 4 moles of H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A dative (coordinate) bond is formed when _____.
options: Both atoms share electrons equally|One atom provides both electrons for the bond|Electrons are transferred|Atoms share unequal numbers of electrons
answer: One atom provides both electrons for the bond
rubric: In a dative (coordinate) covalent bond, one atom (the donor) provides both electrons for the shared bond.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with dilute H₂SO₄?
options: Oxygen|Carbon dioxide|Hydrogen|Sulphur dioxide
rubric: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂; zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What is the general formula of carboxylic acids?
options: R-OH|R-CHO|R-COOH|R-CO-R'
rubric: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group (-COOH) and have the general formula R-COOH.

subject: Biology
stem: The type of blood cell responsible for fighting infections is the _____.
options: Red blood cell|Platelet|White blood cell|Plasma cell
rubric: White blood cells (leucocytes) are part of the immune system and defend the body against infections and foreign bodies.

subject: Biology
stem: The opening and closing of stomata is controlled by _____.
options: Root hairs|Guard cells|Xylem|Epidermis
rubric: Guard cells are paired cells surrounding each stoma; changes in their turgidity control the opening and closing of stomata.

subject: Biology
stem: The carrier of genetic information in most organisms is _____.
options: RNA|Protein|DNA|Lipid
rubric: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is the hereditary molecule in most organisms, carrying genetic instructions for development.

subject: Biology
stem: A food chain always starts with a _____.
options: Consumer|Herbivore|Producer|Decomposer
rubric: All food chains begin with producers (usually green plants) which capture energy from the sun through photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: The process by which a cell divides to produce two identical daughter cells is called _____.
options: Meiosis|Mitosis|Fertilisation|Budding
rubric: Mitosis is the type of cell division producing two genetically identical daughter cells — used for growth and repair.

subject: Biology
stem: The main function of the liver is _____.
options: Pumping blood|Producing insulin|Detoxifying blood and producing bile|Filtering urine
rubric: The liver performs many functions including detoxification of harmful substances, production of bile for digestion, and synthesis of proteins.

subject: Biology
stem: The cell membrane is described as _____.
options: Impermeable|Fully permeable|Selectively permeable|Rigid
rubric: The cell membrane is selectively (semi-)permeable — it controls what enters and exits the cell by allowing some substances through but not others.

subject: Biology
stem: The site of gaseous exchange in the lungs is the _____.
options: Trachea|Bronchi|Alveoli|Larynx
rubric: The alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs with thin walls and a rich blood supply, where O₂ and CO₂ are exchanged.

subject: Biology
stem: Water is transported from roots to leaves through the _____.
options: Phloem|Cambium|Xylem|Epidermis
rubric: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved mineral salts upward from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.

subject: Biology
stem: An organism with two identical alleles for a trait is called _____.
options: Heterozygous|Homozygous|Dominant|Recessive
rubric: A homozygous organism has two identical alleles (e.g. AA or aa) for a particular gene.

subject: Biology
stem: The role of decomposers in an ecosystem is to _____.
options: Produce food|Eat plants|Break down dead matter and recycle nutrients|Capture sunlight
answer: Break down dead matter and recycle nutrients
rubric: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter, releasing nutrients back into the soil for use by producers.

subject: Biology
stem: The enzyme that begins the digestion of starch in the mouth is _____.
options: Pepsin|Trypsin|Amylase|Lipase
rubric: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) in the mouth begins the chemical digestion of starch, breaking it into maltose.

subject: Biology
stem: The female gamete in flowering plants is the _____.
options: Pollen grain|Anther|Ovule|Egg cell
rubric: The egg cell (ovum) is the female gamete in flowering plants, contained within the ovule inside the ovary.

subject: Biology
stem: The process by which water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of high concentration to low is called _____.
options: Active transport|Diffusion|Osmosis|Plasmolysis
rubric: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a semipermeable membrane from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to lower.

subject: Biology
stem: Which blood group is the universal donor?
options: A|B|AB|O
rubric: Blood group O (especially O-negative) is called the universal donor because it lacks A and B antigens, reducing rejection risk.

subject: Biology
stem: Natural selection favours organisms that are _____.
options: Largest|Best adapted to their environment|Fastest|Most colourful
rubric: Natural selection is the process by which organisms with favourable adaptations are more likely to survive and reproduce.

subject: Biology
stem: Photosynthesis requires which of the following inputs?
options: CO₂, H₂O, and light energy|O₂, glucose, and heat|H₂O, O₂, and glucose|CO₂, O₂, and minerals
rubric: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Inputs are carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight.

subject: Biology
stem: The phenotype of an organism is determined by its _____.
options: Genotype only|Environment only|Both genotype and environment|Neither
rubric: Phenotype (observable traits) results from the interaction of an organism's genotype (genetic makeup) with its environment.

subject: Biology
stem: The organelle that packages and transports proteins within the cell is the _____.
options: Lysosome|Golgi apparatus|Ribosome|Mitochondria
rubric: The Golgi apparatus (Golgi body) modifies, packages, and ships proteins and lipids to their final destinations.

subject: Biology
stem: The area where two ecosystems meet and overlap is called a _____.
options: Biome|Ecotone|Niche|Habitat
rubric: An ecotone is a transition zone or boundary between two different ecosystems, containing species from both communities.

subject: Biology
stem: The part of the eye responsible for colour vision is the _____.
options: Cornea|Iris|Rod cells|Cone cells
rubric: Cone cells in the retina are responsible for colour vision and function best in bright light; rod cells detect dim light but not colour.

subject: Biology
stem: The function of insulin in the body is to _____.
options: Increase blood glucose|Decrease blood glucose|Increase heart rate|Stimulate growth
rubric: Insulin, produced by the pancreas, lowers blood glucose by stimulating cells to take up glucose and convert it to glycogen.

subject: Biology
stem: The leaf cells containing most chloroplasts are the _____.
options: Epidermis cells|Palisade mesophyll cells|Spongy mesophyll cells|Guard cells
rubric: Palisade mesophyll cells are tightly packed near the upper surface of leaves and contain the most chloroplasts for efficient photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: If a man (XY) is colour-blind (X^c Y) and a woman is a carrier (X X^c) what fraction of their daughters could be colour-blind?
options: All daughters|None|Half|One quarter
rubric: Daughters receive one X from each parent: X^c from father and X or X^c from mother. Half get X^c X^c (colour-blind).

subject: Biology
stem: Active transport differs from diffusion in that active transport _____.
options: Moves substances from high to low concentration|Requires energy (ATP)|Does not require a membrane|Only moves water
rubric: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient using energy (ATP), unlike passive diffusion.

subject: Biology
stem: The digestion of proteins begins in the _____.
options: Mouth|Oesophagus|Stomach|Small intestine
rubric: Protein digestion begins in the stomach where the enzyme pepsin (activated by HCl) breaks down proteins into peptides.

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following is an abiotic factor?
options: Bacteria|Temperature|Fungi|Plants
rubric: Abiotic factors are non-living physical and chemical aspects of the environment: temperature, light, water, pH, etc.

subject: Biology
stem: The green pigment in plants that absorbs sunlight is _____.
options: Carotene|Xanthophyll|Chlorophyll|Anthocyanin
rubric: Chlorophyll is the primary green pigment in plants that absorbs light energy (mainly red and blue wavelengths) for photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: In Mendel's Law of Segregation alleles _____.
options: Mix together|Separate during gamete formation|Blend with each other|Increase in number
rubric: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that paired alleles separate during the formation of gametes (sex cells).

subject: Biology
stem: The hormone that stimulates the 'fight or flight' response is _____.
options: Insulin|Adrenaline|Oestrogen|Thyroxine
rubric: Adrenaline (epinephrine), produced by the adrenal glands, prepares the body for emergency situations by increasing heart rate and blood flow.

subject: Biology
stem: The process by which light energy is converted to chemical energy in plants is _____.
options: Respiration|Fermentation|Photosynthesis|Transpiration
rubric: Photosynthesis converts light energy (from the sun) into chemical energy stored in glucose molecules.

subject: Biology
stem: External fertilisation is common in _____.
options: Birds|Humans|Frogs|Reptiles
rubric: Frogs and many fish practise external fertilisation — eggs and sperm are released into water where fertilisation occurs.

subject: Biology
stem: An organism that obtains nutrition from another living organism without immediately killing it is a _____.
options: Predator|Parasite|Decomposer|Producer
rubric: A parasite lives on or in a host organism, deriving nutrients from it while usually harming but not immediately killing the host.

subject: Biology
stem: The part of the brain that controls breathing and heart rate is the _____.
options: Cerebrum|Cerebellum|Medulla oblongata|Hypothalamus
rubric: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary vital functions including breathing rate, heart rate, and blood pressure.

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following is NOT an organelle?
options: Mitochondria|Ribosome|Cell membrane|Nucleus
rubric: Organelles are membrane-bound structures within the cell. The cell membrane is the outer boundary of the cell, not an organelle inside it.

subject: Biology
stem: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a mutation in the gene for _____.
options: Insulin|Haemoglobin|Collagen|Amylase
rubric: Sickle cell anaemia results from a single point mutation in the haemoglobin beta-chain gene, producing abnormal haemoglobin S.

subject: Biology
stem: The opening through which gases enter and leave a leaf is called a _____.
options: Lenticel|Stoma|Pore|Cuticle
rubric: Stomata (singular: stoma) are microscopic pores in the leaf epidermis that allow gas exchange (CO₂ in, O₂ out) and water vapour loss.

subject: Biology
stem: The source of all energy in most ecosystems is _____.
options: Water|Soil|The Sun|Wind
rubric: The sun provides the primary energy input to most ecosystems, captured by producers through photosynthesis.

subject: Commerce
stem: An intermediary who buys goods from producers and sells to retailers is a _____.
options: Retailer|Wholesaler|Agent|Consumer
rubric: Wholesalers buy goods in bulk from manufacturers/producers and resell in smaller quantities to retailers.

subject: Commerce
stem: A cheque that has been crossed with two parallel lines can only be _____.
options: Cashed at a counter|Paid into a bank account|Used to buy goods|Exchanged for cash
rubric: A crossed cheque cannot be cashed directly but must be deposited into a bank account, enhancing security.

subject: Commerce
stem: The document that serves as evidence of an insurance contract is the _____.
options: Proposal form|Premium note|Policy|Certificate of insurance
rubric: An insurance policy is the formal contract document outlining the terms, conditions, and coverage of the insurance agreement.

subject: Commerce
stem: The MOST suitable transport for perishable goods over long international distances is _____.
options: Road|Sea|Air|Rail
rubric: Air transport is the fastest mode of transport, making it suitable for perishable goods (food, flowers, pharmaceuticals) over long distances.

subject: Commerce
stem: A document used to correct an overcharge on an invoice is a _____.
options: Debit note|Credit note|Receipt|Statement of account
rubric: A credit note is issued to a buyer when goods are returned or when an overcharge was made — it reduces the amount owed.

subject: Commerce
stem: The difference between the selling price and the cost price of goods is _____.
options: Revenue|Turnover|Gross profit|Net profit
rubric: Gross profit = selling price - cost of goods sold. Net profit additionally deducts operating expenses.

subject: Commerce
stem: A share of a company's profit paid to shareholders is called a _____.
options: Interest|Dividend|Bonus|Commission
rubric: A dividend is the portion of a company's profit distributed to shareholders, usually expressed per share.

subject: Commerce
stem: The advantage of warehousing includes _____.
options: Increasing transport costs|Stabilising prices|Reducing product variety|Limiting supply
rubric: Warehousing allows goods to be stored and released gradually, preventing gluts and shortages that cause price fluctuations.

subject: Commerce
stem: The fastest form of modern business communication is _____.
options: Letter|Telex|Telephone|Email/Internet
rubric: Email and internet-based communications are near-instantaneous, making them the fastest forms of modern business communication.

subject: Commerce
stem: International trade differs from home trade in that it involves _____.
options: More consumers|Use of currency|Trade across national borders|More products
rubric: International trade (foreign trade) involves buying and selling between countries, whereas home trade is within one country.

subject: Commerce
stem: The premium in insurance is the _____.
options: Amount paid as compensation|Profit of the insurer|Regular payment made by the insured|Value of the insured item
answer: Regular payment made by the insured
rubric: The premium is the periodic amount paid by the insured to the insurance company in exchange for coverage.

subject: Commerce
stem: A fixed deposit account differs from a savings account in that _____.
options: It earns no interest|Money is deposited for a fixed period at a fixed rate|You can withdraw at any time|It has no minimum balance
answer: Money is deposited for a fixed period at a fixed rate
rubric: Fixed (time) deposits lock in funds for a specified period at an agreed interest rate, usually higher than savings accounts.

subject: Commerce
stem: A consumer cooperative society is formed to _____.
options: Maximise profits for shareholders|Buy goods cheaply in bulk for members|Employ as many workers as possible|Compete with supermarkets
answer: Buy goods cheaply in bulk for members
rubric: Consumer cooperatives buy goods in bulk at wholesale prices and sell to members at reduced prices, sharing any surplus.

subject: Commerce
stem: The balance of payments records a country's _____.
options: Only exports and imports|All financial transactions with the rest of the world|Only foreign loans|Government spending
answer: All financial transactions with the rest of the world
rubric: The balance of payments is a comprehensive record of all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world over a period.

subject: Commerce
stem: Working capital is defined as _____.
options: Fixed assets minus liabilities|Current assets minus current liabilities|Total assets minus total liabilities|Long-term assets only
rubric: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities. It measures a business's short-term liquidity.

subject: Commerce
stem: Which of the following is an advantage of road transport?
options: Carries very heavy loads|Door-to-door delivery|Fastest over long distances|Cheapest per ton-km
rubric: Road transport offers the advantage of door-to-door delivery, providing flexibility that rail and sea transport cannot match.

subject: Commerce
stem: A document sent by a buyer to a seller requesting the supply of goods is a _____.
options: Invoice|Purchase order|Delivery note|Bill of lading
rubric: A purchase order is sent by the buyer to the seller specifying goods required, quantities, and agreed prices.

subject: Commerce
stem: E-banking (electronic banking) allows customers to _____.
options: Visit the bank physically|Conduct banking transactions online|Apply for physical bank cards only|Talk to bank staff only
rubric: E-banking allows customers to access and manage their accounts, transfer funds, and pay bills online without visiting a branch.

subject: Commerce
stem: Cold storage is used for _____.
options: Furniture|Perishable goods|Machinery|Textiles
rubric: Cold storage (refrigerated warehousing) is used to preserve perishable goods like food, medicine, and flowers at low temperatures.

subject: Commerce
stem: The principle of subrogation in insurance means that _____.
options: The insured can insure the same item twice|After paying a claim, the insurer takes over the insured's rights against a third party|The insured must pay the premium|The insurer can cancel the policy anytime
answer: After paying a claim, the insurer takes over the insured's rights against a third party
rubric: Subrogation allows the insurer to stand in the shoes of the insured and claim from a third party who caused the loss.

subject: Commerce
stem: Advertising is primarily aimed at _____.
options: Reducing production costs|Informing and persuading consumers to buy|Training employees|Managing accounts
answer: Informing and persuading consumers to buy
rubric: Advertising informs potential customers about products/services and persuades them to purchase, stimulating demand.

subject: Commerce
stem: The function of a commercial bank includes _____.
options: Issuing currency|Setting interest rates|Accepting deposits and granting loans|Controlling inflation
rubric: The primary functions of a commercial bank are to accept deposits from customers and grant loans to borrowers.

subject: Commerce
stem: Equity capital in a limited company is obtained through _____.
options: Bank loans|Issuing shares|Government grants|Trade credit
rubric: Equity (share) capital is raised by a company issuing shares to investors who become part-owners (shareholders) of the company.

subject: Commerce
stem: A sole proprietorship has the disadvantage of _____.
options: Shared decision-making|Unlimited liability|Limited working hours|Shared profits
rubric: In a sole proprietorship, the owner has unlimited liability — personal assets can be used to settle business debts.

subject: Commerce
stem: Containerisation has improved sea transport by _____.
options: Reducing ship size|Speeding loading and reducing theft and damage|Increasing port charges|Eliminating road transport
answer: Speeding loading and reducing theft and damage
rubric: Containerisation allows standardised sealed containers to be loaded quickly and securely, reducing theft, damage, and handling time.

subject: Commerce
stem: The insurable interest principle requires that the insured must _____.
options: Know the insurer personally|Stand to suffer financial loss if the insured event occurs|Pay the highest premium possible|Own the insurance company
answer: Stand to suffer financial loss if the insured event occurs
rubric: Insurable interest means the insured must have a financial stake in the subject matter — they must suffer a monetary loss if the event occurs.

subject: Commerce
stem: A document showing all transactions between a buyer and a seller over a period is a _____.
options: Invoice|Receipt|Statement of account|Delivery note
rubric: A statement of account is a periodic summary sent by a seller to a buyer showing all invoices, payments, and the balance owed.

subject: Commerce
stem: Depreciation is the _____.
options: Increase in asset value over time|Decrease in asset value over time|Interest on loans|Cost of buying assets
answer: Decrease in asset value over time
rubric: Depreciation is the systematic reduction in the recorded value of an asset over time due to use, wear and tear, or obsolescence.

subject: Commerce
stem: A market where goods are bought and sold using electronic platforms is called _____.
options: Black market|Physical market|E-commerce market|Commodity market
rubric: E-commerce involves buying and selling goods and services over the internet through electronic platforms.

subject: Commerce
stem: The term 'caveat emptor' means _____.
options: Let the seller beware|Let the buyer beware|Both parties must agree|Price is negotiable
rubric: Caveat emptor is a Latin legal phrase meaning 'let the buyer beware' — buyers purchase at their own risk.

subject: Commerce
stem: An overdraft facility allows a customer to _____.
options: Save more money|Withdraw more than the account balance|Earn higher interest|Transfer funds abroad
answer: Withdraw more than the account balance
rubric: An overdraft allows a current account holder to withdraw funds in excess of their account balance, up to an agreed limit.

subject: Commerce
stem: Cabotage policy in shipping refers to _____.
options: International shipping rights|Restricting coastal trade to national vessels|Free movement of ships|Taxing all imports
answer: Restricting coastal trade to national vessels
rubric: Cabotage laws reserve coastal or internal waterway shipping routes for vessels registered in that country.

subject: Commerce
stem: An airway bill (air waybill) is used in _____.
options: Rail transport|Sea transport|Air transport|Road transport
rubric: An air waybill (AWB) is the contract of carriage for goods transported by air, serving as both the receipt and shipping document.

subject: Commerce
stem: Re-insurance means _____.
options: Cancelling an insurance policy|An insurer taking out insurance with another insurer to spread risk|Paying the premium twice|Insuring goods after loss
answer: An insurer taking out insurance with another insurer to spread risk
rubric: Re-insurance is when an insurance company transfers portions of its risk portfolios to other insurers to reduce the chance of paying a large obligation.

subject: Commerce
stem: The Hire Purchase system involves _____.
options: Paying full price upfront|Making a down payment and paying the rest in instalments while using the good|Renting without owning|Borrowing money without repayment
answer: Making a down payment and paying the rest in instalments while using the good
rubric: In hire purchase, the buyer pays an initial deposit and the balance (plus interest) in instalments; ownership transfers on final payment.

subject: Commerce
stem: A cartel is _____.
options: A single large company|A group of firms that agree to fix prices and limit competition|A government trading body|An international aid organisation
answer: A group of firms that agree to fix prices and limit competition
rubric: A cartel is an agreement among competing businesses to coordinate pricing or output to reduce competition, like OPEC in the oil industry.

subject: Commerce
stem: Branding helps businesses by _____.
options: Reducing production costs|Creating product recognition and loyalty|Limiting the number of consumers|Eliminating advertising needs
rubric: Branding creates an identifiable name, symbol, or design that distinguishes a product, building consumer recognition and loyalty.

subject: Commerce
stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)?
options: Issuing currency|Lender of last resort|Accepting deposits from the public|Regulating commercial banks
rubric: The CBN does not accept deposits from the general public. Commercial banks do that. The CBN serves banks and the government.

subject: Commerce
stem: Free trade refers to _____.
options: Goods given away freely|Trade without restrictions between countries|Domestic trade only|Trade in free goods only
rubric: Free trade is a policy allowing goods and services to be traded between countries without tariffs, quotas, or other restrictions.

subject: Commerce
stem: The memorandum of association of a company contains its _____.
options: Internal rules|External objectives and relationship with the outside world|Employment contracts|Banking details
answer: External objectives and relationship with the outside world
rubric: The memorandum of association defines the company's name, objectives, share capital, and its external relationships.

subject: Economics
stem: A good whose demand falls as income increases is called a _____.
options: Normal good|Veblen good|Inferior good|Luxury good
rubric: Inferior goods have a negative income elasticity of demand — as income rises, consumers buy less and switch to better alternatives.

subject: Economics
stem: The short run in economics is defined as a period when _____.
options: All factors are variable|At least one factor of production is fixed|Output cannot change|No production occurs
answer: At least one factor of production is fixed
rubric: In the short run, at least one input (typically capital/land) cannot be changed; in the long run, all inputs can vary.

subject: Economics
stem: A monopoly exists when _____.
options: Many firms sell identical goods|One firm controls the entire supply of a product|A few large firms dominate|Firms compete on price
answer: One firm controls the entire supply of a product
rubric: A monopoly is a market structure with a single seller who has no close substitutes and significant market power.

subject: Economics
stem: When the Central Bank reduces the minimum rediscount rate commercial banks will likely _____.
options: Increase interest rates|Reduce lending|Lend more money at lower rates|Stop borrowing from CBN
answer: Lend more money at lower rates
rubric: A lower minimum rediscount rate reduces the cost of borrowing from the central bank, encouraging commercial banks to borrow more and lend at lower rates.

subject: Economics
stem: A tariff is _____.
options: A ban on imports|A tax on imported goods|A trade agreement|A shipping document
rubric: A tariff is a tax levied by governments on imported goods, making foreign products more expensive and protecting domestic industries.

subject: Economics
stem: Gross National Product (GNP) differs from GDP in that GNP _____.
options: Excludes government spending|Includes income earned by citizens abroad|Only counts manufacturing|Includes only exports
answer: Includes income earned by citizens abroad
rubric: GNP = GDP + income earned by residents abroad - income earned by foreigners domestically. It measures national output regardless of location.

subject: Economics
stem: When supply increases and demand remains constant the equilibrium price will _____.
options: Rise|Fall|Stay the same|Become zero
rubric: An increase in supply (shift right) with unchanged demand leads to a surplus at the old price, pushing the equilibrium price down.

subject: Economics
stem: The profit motive is most associated with _____.
options: Socialism|Command economy|Mixed economy|Capitalism
rubric: Capitalism is characterised by private ownership of the means of production and the profit motive as the primary driver of economic activity.

subject: Economics
stem: The reward for labour as a factor of production is _____.
options: Rent|Profit|Wages|Interest
rubric: The four factors of production and their rewards: Land → Rent; Labour → Wages; Capital → Interest; Entrepreneurship → Profit.

subject: Economics
stem: Direct taxes are levied on _____.
options: Goods and services|Income and wealth|Imports only|Exports only
rubric: Direct taxes (e.g. income tax, company tax) are levied directly on income or wealth; indirect taxes are on goods and services.

subject: Economics
stem: The law of supply states that an increase in price leads to _____.
options: A fall in supply|A rise in quantity supplied|No change|A rise in demand
rubric: The law of supply: ceteris paribus, as price rises, producers are willing to supply more, creating a positive price-quantity relationship.

subject: Economics
stem: Economies of scale refer to _____.
options: Cost reduction per unit as output increases|Higher costs for large firms|Fixed costs of production|The scale of a country's economy
answer: Cost reduction per unit as output increases
rubric: Economies of scale occur when increasing production reduces the average (per unit) cost due to efficiencies of large-scale production.

subject: Economics
stem: Price elasticity of demand is measured as _____.
options: % change in price / % change in supply|% change in quantity demanded / % change in price|% change in income / % change in demand|% change in supply / % change in price
answer: % change in quantity demanded / % change in price
rubric: PED = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price). A value > 1 = elastic; < 1 = inelastic.

subject: Economics
stem: The terms of trade measure _____.
options: The volume of exports|The ratio of export prices to import prices|Trade restrictions|The balance of payments
answer: The ratio of export prices to import prices
rubric: Terms of trade = (index of export prices / index of import prices) × 100. Improvement means exports buy more imports.

subject: Economics
stem: A price ceiling is set _____.
options: Above the equilibrium price|Below the equilibrium price|At the equilibrium price|At a random level
rubric: A price ceiling (maximum price) is set below the equilibrium to make goods affordable, but it often causes shortages.

subject: Economics
stem: Oligopoly is characterised by _____.
options: One seller|Two sellers|A few large sellers|Many small sellers
rubric: Oligopoly is a market structure dominated by a small number of large firms (e.g. telecoms, oil companies).

subject: Economics
stem: Urbanisation refers to _____.
options: Decrease in city populations|Movement of people from rural to urban areas|Growth of farming communities|Reduction in urban poverty
answer: Movement of people from rural to urban areas
rubric: Urbanisation is the increasing proportion of a population living in urban areas (cities and towns) relative to rural areas.

subject: Economics
stem: The opportunity cost of a decision is _____.
options: The total money spent|The value of the next best alternative forgone|The profit gained|The loss incurred
answer: The value of the next best alternative forgone
rubric: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative you give up when making a choice — a fundamental economic concept.

subject: Economics
stem: Per capita income is calculated as _____.
options: National income|National income × population|National income / population|Population / national income
rubric: Per capita income = National income / Total population. It indicates the average income per person.

subject: Economics
stem: Inflation is defined as _____.
options: A fall in the value of money|A sustained rise in the general price level|A fall in imports|A rise in wages only
answer: A sustained rise in the general price level
rubric: Inflation is a persistent and general increase in the price level of goods and services, reducing purchasing power.

subject: Economics
stem: Subsistence agriculture is characterised by _____.
options: Large-scale commercial production|Growing food mainly for personal consumption|Use of heavy machinery|Large surpluses for export
answer: Growing food mainly for personal consumption
rubric: Subsistence farming produces just enough food to feed the farmer's family with little or no surplus for sale.

subject: Economics
stem: A substitute good for tea is most likely _____.
options: Sugar|Coffee|Milk|Teacup
rubric: Substitute goods satisfy the same need; a rise in tea prices increases demand for coffee as consumers switch to the cheaper alternative.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following causes a shift in the demand curve?
options: Change in price|Change in consumer income|Change in quantity demanded|Change in supply
rubric: A change in price causes movement along the demand curve; a change in income (or other factors) shifts the entire curve.

subject: Economics
stem: Fixed costs are costs that _____.
options: Vary with output|Do not change with level of output|Are always zero|Equal marginal cost
answer: Do not change with level of output
rubric: Fixed costs (e.g. rent, insurance) remain constant regardless of how much is produced in the short run.

subject: Economics
stem: Perfect competition is characterised by _____.
options: Product differentiation|Price-setting power|Homogeneous products and price-taking|High barriers to entry
rubric: In perfect competition, all firms sell identical products and must accept the market price (price-takers); no single firm influences price.

subject: Economics
stem: Fiscal policy involves _____.
options: Controlling money supply|Government spending and taxation|Interest rate management|Exchange rate policy
rubric: Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy's performance.

subject: Economics
stem: Comparative advantage theory was developed by _____.
options: Adam Smith|David Ricardo|John Maynard Keynes|Alfred Marshall
rubric: David Ricardo's theory of comparative advantage (1817) explains why countries benefit from specialising in goods they produce at relatively lower opportunity cost.

subject: Economics
stem: The minimum wage is an example of a _____.
options: Price ceiling|Price floor|Quota|Subsidy
rubric: A minimum wage sets a legal minimum that employers must pay workers — it is a price floor (set above the equilibrium wage) to protect workers.

subject: Economics
stem: Net National Product (NNP) is calculated as _____.
options: GNP + depreciation|GNP - depreciation|GNP + taxes|GNP - subsidies
rubric: NNP = GNP - depreciation (capital consumption allowance). It adjusts for the wear and tear of capital assets.

subject: Economics
stem: When the value of a country's currency falls relative to others this is called _____.
options: Appreciation|Depreciation|Devaluation|Inflation
rubric: Currency depreciation is the fall in a currency's value relative to other currencies in a floating exchange rate system.

subject: Economics
stem: Complementary goods are goods that _____.
options: Compete with each other|Are used together|Replace each other|Have no relationship
rubric: Complementary goods are consumed together (e.g. cars and petrol, bread and butter) — a rise in price of one reduces demand for both.

subject: Economics
stem: The main economic problem in every society is _____.
options: Unemployment|Scarcity of resources|Inflation|Poverty
rubric: Scarcity — the fundamental economic problem — arises because unlimited human wants cannot all be met with limited resources.

subject: Economics
stem: Capital as a factor of production refers to _____.
options: Money in a bank|Man-made resources used in production|Land and natural resources|Labour
rubric: In economics, capital refers to man-made goods (machines, tools, factories) used to produce other goods and services.

subject: Economics
stem: A perfectly inelastic demand curve is _____.
options: Horizontal|Upward sloping|Vertical|Downward sloping
rubric: A vertical demand curve represents perfectly inelastic demand — quantity demanded does not change regardless of price.

subject: Economics
stem: Economic development is different from economic growth because development includes _____.
options: Only GDP increase|Improvements in human welfare and living standards|Only industrial output|Only export earnings
answer: Improvements in human welfare and living standards
rubric: Economic development encompasses not just output growth (GDP) but also improvements in living standards, education, health, and equity.

subject: Economics
stem: The narrow definition of money supply (M1) includes _____.
options: Currency and demand deposits|All bank deposits|Treasury bills|Foreign exchange
rubric: M1 (narrow money) consists of currency in circulation plus demand deposits (current accounts) that can be used directly for transactions.

subject: Government
stem: The 1999 Constitution was enacted under which Nigerian military head of state?
options: Sani Abacha|Ibrahim Babangida|Abdulsalami Abubakar|Murtala Mohammed
rubric: The 1999 Constitution was promulgated by General Abdulsalami Abubakar's military government during the transition to civilian rule.

subject: Government
stem: Which of the following is a feature of a democratic government?
options: One-party rule|Free and fair elections|Suppression of opposition|Rule by force
rubric: Democracy is characterised by free and fair elections, universal suffrage, civil liberties, and the rule of law.

subject: Government
stem: A unitary system of government concentrates power in the _____.
options: State governments|Local governments|Central government|Military
rubric: In a unitary state, sovereign power rests with the central government; regional governments are subordinate to it.

subject: Government
stem: The principle of meritocracy in the civil service means _____.
options: Appointments based on personal connections|Appointments based on competence and merit|Promotions based on age|Appointments made by politicians
answer: Appointments based on competence and merit
rubric: Meritocracy ensures that civil servants are recruited and promoted based on ability, qualifications, and performance, not favouritism.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria's president is also the _____.
options: Speaker of the house|Commander-in-chief of the armed forces|Chief Justice|Senate President
rubric: The Nigerian Constitution designates the President as the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federation.

subject: Government
stem: The social contract theory of government was associated with _____.
options: Karl Marx|John Locke and Rousseau|Adolf Hitler|Napoleon Bonaparte
rubric: Social contract theorists (Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau) argued that governments derive their authority from an agreement (contract) with the governed.

subject: Government
stem: A by-election is held when _____.
options: There is a general election|A legislative seat becomes vacant|A president is impeached|A referendum is called
rubric: A by-election is held to fill a vacant legislative seat between general elections, caused by death, resignation, or disqualification.

subject: Government
stem: The United Nations was established in _____.
rubric: The United Nations (UN) was founded on 24 October 1945 after World War II to maintain international peace and security.

subject: Government
stem: The power of the Nigerian Senate to confirm presidential appointments is an example of _____.
options: Federalism|Separation of powers|Checks and balances|Judicial review
rubric: The confirmation power of the Senate over executive appointments is a mechanism of checks and balances, preventing concentration of power.

subject: Government
stem: Sovereignty means _____.
options: Economic power|Supreme authority to govern without external interference|Military strength|International recognition
answer: Supreme authority to govern without external interference
rubric: Sovereignty is the full right and power of a state to govern itself without any interference from outside sources.

subject: Government
stem: Which document is regarded as the international bill of human rights?
options: African Charter|Geneva Convention|Universal Declaration of Human Rights|ECOWAS Treaty
rubric: The UDHR was adopted by the UN in 1948 and sets out fundamental human rights to be universally protected.

subject: Government
stem: Proportional representation is an electoral system where _____.
options: The winner takes all|Seats are allocated based on the share of votes won|Only parties can contest|Only two parties compete
answer: Seats are allocated based on the share of votes won
rubric: Proportional representation allocates parliamentary seats to parties in proportion to their share of the popular vote.

subject: Government
stem: Which tier of government in Nigeria has responsibility for primary education?
options: Federal|State|Local|None
rubric: Under Nigeria's constitution, primary education is on the concurrent list but is primarily administered by Local Government Areas.

subject: Government
stem: Cabinet government is associated with _____.
options: Presidential system|Parliamentary system|Military rule|Confederation
rubric: In a parliamentary system, the Cabinet (executive) is drawn from and accountable to the legislature — it is the hallmark of cabinet government.

subject: Government
stem: Pressure groups differ from political parties in that pressure groups _____.
options: Contest elections|Do not seek political power directly|Rule the country|Make laws
answer: Do not seek political power directly
rubric: Pressure groups (interest groups) seek to influence government policy without contesting elections or seeking to govern.

subject: Government
stem: The Commonwealth of Nations is headquartered in _____.
options: New York|Addis Ababa|London|Brussels
rubric: The Commonwealth Secretariat is based at Marlborough House in London, UK.

subject: Government
stem: Which of the following items is on the concurrent legislative list in Nigeria?
options: Defence|Foreign affairs|Education|External borrowing
rubric: Education is on the concurrent list, meaning both federal and state governments can legislate on it; states mainly administer primary and secondary education.

subject: Government
stem: Emergency powers can be invoked by the Nigerian president to _____.
options: Extend his term indefinitely|Temporarily suspend certain rights during a crisis|Dismiss the judiciary|Override the constitution entirely
answer: Temporarily suspend certain rights during a crisis
rubric: Emergency powers allow the President to take extraordinary measures during a crisis, including limiting some rights, subject to National Assembly approval.

subject: Government
stem: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) was established by the _____.
options: Police Act|Electoral Act|1999 Constitution|Presidential Decree
rubric: INEC was established under the provisions of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: A political party's platform refers to its _____.
options: Headquarters building|Statement of goals and policies|Campaign funding|Membership list
rubric: A political party's platform (or manifesto) is its official statement of values, goals, and proposed policies if elected.

subject: Government
stem: The doctrine of collective responsibility means that cabinet ministers _____.
options: Each act independently|Support government decisions in public even if they disagreed in private|Can criticise government publicly|Are not responsible to parliament
answer: Support government decisions in public even if they disagreed in private
rubric: Collective cabinet responsibility means ministers must publicly support cabinet decisions; those who cannot resign must do so.

subject: Government
stem: Recall of a senator in Nigeria requires a petition signed by more than _____ of registered voters in the constituency.
rubric: The Nigerian Constitution provides that a senator may be recalled by a simple majority (over half) of registered voters in his/her constituency signing a petition.

subject: Government
stem: The purpose of NATO is _____.
options: Economic cooperation|Military collective defence|Cultural exchange|Environmental protection
rubric: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is a military alliance where members commit to collective defence — an attack on one is treated as an attack on all.

subject: Government
stem: The Electoral Act regulating Nigeria's elections is passed by the _____.
options: INEC|President|National Assembly|Supreme Court
rubric: Electoral laws are made by the National Assembly (the federal legislature) in Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: Proportional representation promotes _____.
options: Two-party systems|Multi-party representation|Winner-takes-all outcomes|Military involvement
rubric: Proportional representation tends to produce multi-party legislatures that more closely reflect the diversity of voter preferences.

subject: Government
stem: The Chief Justice of Nigeria is appointed by _____.
options: The President alone|The National Judicial Council on the recommendation of the President subject to Senate confirmation|The Senate only|The State Governors
answer: The National Judicial Council on the recommendation of the President subject to Senate confirmation
rubric: The CJN is appointed on the recommendation of the NJC, forwarded by the President, and confirmed by the Senate.

subject: Government
stem: Delegated legislation refers to _____.
options: Laws made by the legislature|Laws made by local government|Secondary laws made by bodies to whom Parliament has delegated authority|International treaties
answer: Secondary laws made by bodies to whom Parliament has delegated authority
rubric: Delegated (secondary) legislation is law made by ministers, local authorities, or other bodies under powers granted to them by an Act of Parliament.

subject: Government
stem: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of democracy?
options: Periodic elections|Military dictatorship|Separation of powers|Rule of law
rubric: Democracy is built on free elections, separation of powers, rule of law, and civil liberties. Military dictatorship is antithetical to democracy.

subject: Government
stem: The Nigerian House of Representatives has _____ members.
rubric: The House of Representatives consists of 360 members elected from single-member constituencies across Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: The residual powers in Nigeria's federal system belong to _____.
options: Federal government|State governments|Local governments|Judiciary
rubric: Residual powers (matters not listed on exclusive or concurrent lists) are exercised by the 36 state governments.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria is a member of which of the following international organisations?
options: NATO|ASEAN|ECOWAS|SAARC
rubric: Nigeria is a founding and leading member of ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States), established in 1975.

subject: Government
stem: Civil society refers to _____.
options: The military|Non-governmental organisations and citizens outside the state and market|Only political parties|Government agencies
answer: Non-governmental organisations and citizens outside the state and market
rubric: Civil society comprises NGOs, trade unions, religious bodies, professional associations, and voluntary organisations that operate between the family and the state.

subject: Government
stem: The Nigerian Senate is composed of _____ senators.
rubric: The Nigerian Senate has 109 members: three senators from each of the 36 states plus one for the Federal Capital Territory.

subject: Government
stem: The Secret ballot system ensures _____.
options: That all votes are counted twice|That votes cannot be traced back to individuals|That only educated people vote|That results are announced immediately
answer: That votes cannot be traced back to individuals
rubric: The secret ballot protects voter privacy by ensuring that no one can determine how an individual voted, preventing intimidation.

subject: Government
stem: The main advantage of a federal system of government is _____.
options: Concentration of power|Uniform policies nationwide|Accommodation of diversity and regional differences|Faster decision-making
answer: Accommodation of diversity and regional differences
rubric: Federalism allows diverse groups (ethnic, cultural, regional) to govern themselves locally while remaining part of a larger national entity.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The conflict between the individual and society is a major theme in _____.
options: Death and the King's Horseman|A Midsummer Night's Dream|Macbeth|Julius Caesar
rubric: Wole Soyinka's Death and the King's Horseman explores the clash between Yoruba tradition (Elesin's duty to die) and colonial/Western society.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An ode is a type of poem that _____.
options: Tells a story|Expresses grief|Celebrates or addresses a subject with deep feeling|Has exactly 14 lines
answer: Celebrates or addresses a subject with deep feeling
rubric: An ode is a lyric poem in praise of or addressed to a person, thing, or idea, often with elevated language.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Dramatic irony occurs when _____.
options: The audience knows something a character does not|A character says one thing but means another|Two events happen at once|The author directly addresses the reader
answer: The audience knows something a character does not
rubric: Dramatic irony is when the audience has knowledge that a character in the story or play lacks, creating tension or humour.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The narrative technique in which the narrator is a character in the story is called _____ person narration.
options: Third|Second|First|Zero
rubric: First-person narration uses 'I' — the narrator is a character in the story, offering an intimate subjective viewpoint.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Onomatopoeia is the use of words that _____.
options: Contradict each other|Imitate the sounds they describe|Exaggerate a point|Compare two unlike things
rubric: Onomatopoeia describes words whose pronunciation resembles the sound they denote: buzz, hiss, crack, splash.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in a poem is called _____.
options: Rhyme|Rhythm|Metre|Stanza
rubric: Metre is the systematic arrangement of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse, giving poetry its musical quality.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A play within a play is a technique used in _____.
options: Things Fall Apart|Hamlet|Arrow of God|Weep Not Child
rubric: Hamlet by Shakespeare features a play-within-a-play (The Mousetrap) that Hamlet uses to confirm Claudius's guilt.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The 'stream of consciousness' technique in fiction directly represents _____.
options: A character's physical actions|A character's random flow of thoughts and feelings|A chronological plot|Historical events
answer: A character's random flow of thoughts and feelings
rubric: Stream of consciousness is a narrative technique portraying a character's unfiltered, continuous flow of thoughts and perceptions.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Antithesis is a figure of speech that _____.
options: Repeats sounds|Places contrasting ideas side by side|Overstates something|Understates something
answer: Places contrasting ideas side by side
rubric: Antithesis juxtaposes contrasting ideas in parallel grammatical structures — e.g. 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Blank verse is verse written in _____.
options: Rhyming couplets|Free verse with no rules|Unrhymed iambic pentameter|Haiku form
rubric: Blank verse has regular iambic pentameter (10 syllables per line, alternating stress) but no end rhyme; Shakespeare used it extensively.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The author of 'Weep Not Child' is _____.
options: Chinua Achebe|Ngugi wa Thiong'o|Wole Soyinka|Cyprian Ekwensi
rubric: Weep Not Child (1964) by Ngugi wa Thiong'o is the first East African novel in English, set during the Mau Mau rebellion in Kenya.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An extended metaphor that runs through an entire poem or prose work is called an _____.
options: Allegory|Allusion|Symbolism|Irony
rubric: An allegory is a work in which characters and events symbolise deeper meanings — an extended metaphor across an entire narrative.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Catharsis in drama refers to _____.
options: The climax of the play|The emotional release felt by the audience|The villain's defeat|The final scene
answer: The emotional release felt by the audience
rubric: Aristotle's concept of catharsis describes the purging of emotions (especially pity and fear) that audiences experience at the end of a tragedy.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In a novel the narrative perspective through which events are filtered is called the _____.
options: Plot|Setting|Point of view|Conflict
rubric: Point of view (narrative perspective) refers to the vantage point from which a story is told — first, second, or third person.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Euphemism is the use of _____.
options: Harsh direct language|Mild or indirect language to avoid bluntness|Exaggerated language|Foreign language
answer: Mild or indirect language to avoid bluntness
rubric: Euphemism substitutes an inoffensive word or phrase for one that might give offence — e.g. 'passed away' for 'died'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A poem of mourning or lamentation for the dead is called an _____.
options: Epic|Ode|Elegy|Ballad
rubric: An elegy is a mournful, contemplative poem written to mourn the death of a person or to reflect on serious loss.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Achebe's Arrow of God is set in which fictional Igbo clan?
options: Umuofia|Umuaro|Abame|Ogidi
rubric: Arrow of God (1964) is set in Umuaro, a fictional Igbo clan in colonial Nigeria, following the Chief Priest Ezeulu.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The part of a play that provides background information is the _____.
options: Climax|Falling action|Exposition|Resolution
rubric: The exposition introduces the setting, characters, and background information at the beginning of a play or narrative.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Which of the following is an example of a metaphor?
options: She is as brave as a lion|Life is a journey|The wind whispered|She runs very fast
rubric: A metaphor makes a direct comparison without using 'like' or 'as': 'Life is a journey' equates life to a journey directly.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The repetition of vowel sounds within words in a line of poetry is called _____.
options: Alliteration|Rhyme|Assonance|Consonance
rubric: Assonance is the repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words — e.g. 'The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The turning point or highest point of tension in a narrative is the _____.
options: Exposition|Rising action|Climax|Denouement
rubric: The climax is the most intense, exciting, or important point in a narrative — the turning point from which the action resolves.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In Greek tragedy the fatal flaw of the hero is called _____.
options: Catharsis|Nemesis|Hamartia|Hubris
rubric: Hamartia is the tragic flaw or error in judgement that leads to the downfall of the tragic hero in Greek drama.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Soyinka's 'The Lion and the Jewel' contrasts _____.
options: Tradition and modernity|War and peace|Love and hate|Youth and old age
rubric: The Lion and the Jewel dramatises the conflict between African tradition (represented by Baroka) and Western modernity (represented by Lakunle).

subject: Literature in English
stem: Pathetic fallacy is _____.
options: The attribution of human emotions to nature or inanimate objects|A logical error|An exaggeration|A type of rhyme
answer: The attribution of human emotions to nature or inanimate objects
rubric: Pathetic fallacy attributes human emotions to the weather or nature — e.g. 'the angry sea' or 'weeping willows'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The volta in a sonnet is _____.
options: The opening line|The rhyme scheme|The turn or shift in argument|The final couplet
answer: The turn or shift in argument
rubric: The volta is the thematic or argumentative turn in a sonnet, often occurring at line 9 in a Petrarchan sonnet.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A bildungsroman is a novel about _____.
options: War and conflict|The growth and development of a young person|A detective story|Historical events
answer: The growth and development of a young person
rubric: A bildungsroman (coming-of-age novel) traces the moral, psychological, and social development of its protagonist from youth to adulthood.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The stage direction 'aside' in drama indicates that _____.
options: All characters speak together|A character speaks to the audience unheard by other characters|A character exits|A character whispers to another
answer: A character speaks to the audience unheard by other characters
rubric: An aside is a remark made directly to the audience, convention holding that other characters on stage cannot hear it.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Ama Ata Aidoo is a writer from _____.
options: Nigeria|Kenya|Ghana|South Africa
rubric: Ama Ata Aidoo is a celebrated Ghanaian writer, playwright, and poet known for works like 'Our Sister Killjoy'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Bathos is _____.
options: A sudden descent from the sublime to the trivial|A build-up of tension|A dramatic climax|A figure of repetition
answer: A sudden descent from the sublime to the trivial
rubric: Bathos is an abrupt, jarring transition from an elevated topic to something trivial or disappointing, creating a comic or ironic effect.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Sprung rhythm is a metrical innovation associated with which poet?
options: W.B. Yeats|T.S. Eliot|Gerard Manley Hopkins|John Keats
rubric: Gerard Manley Hopkins invented 'sprung rhythm' — a system measuring lines by the number of stressed syllables, regardless of unstressed ones.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Dramatic irony in Sophocles' Oedipus Rex is evident when _____.
options: Oedipus kills Laius|The chorus sings|Oedipus investigates a crime the audience knows he himself committed|Jocasta dies
answer: Oedipus investigates a crime the audience knows he himself committed
rubric: The Greek audience knew the myth: Oedipus unknowingly killed his father and married his mother, creating powerful dramatic irony throughout.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Flash-forward (prolepsis) in fiction is _____.
options: A recollection of past events|A jump ahead in time to show future events|A repeated scene|A change in narrator
answer: A jump ahead in time to show future events
rubric: Prolepsis (flash-forward) is a narrative technique where the story jumps ahead in time, anticipating future events.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Which Nigerian author wrote 'Purple Hibiscus'?
options: Wole Soyinka|Ben Okri|Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie|Buchi Emecheta
rubric: Purple Hibiscus (2003) is Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's debut novel set in post-colonial Nigeria.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A paradox is a statement that _____.
options: Is obviously true|Seems contradictory but reveals a deeper truth|Makes no sense at all|Is a direct comparison
answer: Seems contradictory but reveals a deeper truth
rubric: A paradox appears self-contradictory but contains a truth on deeper examination — e.g. 'Less is more'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A soliloquy differs from a monologue in that a soliloquy is _____.
options: Spoken to another character|Spoken aloud to reveal inner thoughts when alone|A long speech to the audience|A dialogue
answer: Spoken aloud to reveal inner thoughts when alone
rubric: A soliloquy is spoken by a character alone on stage, revealing private thoughts to the audience; a monologue can be spoken to others.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The ballad stanza typically has the rhyme scheme _____.
options: ABAB|ABBA|AABB|ABCB
rubric: The traditional ballad stanza has four lines with a rhyme scheme of ABCB — the second and fourth lines rhyme.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Magical realism is a literary style associated with _____.
options: Historical fiction|Realistic settings with magical or supernatural elements|Horror fiction|Science fiction only
answer: Realistic settings with magical or supernatural elements
rubric: Magical realism blends realistic narrative with fantastical elements presented as ordinary, famously used by Gabriel García Márquez and Ben Okri.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Which of these is a collection of poetry by Wole Soyinka?
options: Beware Soul Brother|Idanre and Other Poems|Christmas in Biafra|The Voice
rubric: Idanre and Other Poems (1967) is Wole Soyinka's first full poetry collection, reflecting Yoruba mythology.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The unities in classical drama refer to _____.
options: Unity of characters|Unity of action, time, and place|Unity of theme|Unity of language
answer: Unity of action, time, and place
rubric: The three classical unities (derived from Aristotle): a play should have one main plot (action), occur within one day (time), and in one location (place).

subject: Literature in English
stem: Zeugma is a figure of speech in which one word governs or modifies _____.
options: One word only|Multiple words in different ways|Repetition of a phrase|Words with the same sound
rubric: Zeugma uses one word to modify or govern two or more others in a syntactically parallel but semantically different way — e.g. 'She opened her door and her heart'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An anti-hero is a protagonist who _____.
options: Has conventional heroic qualities|Lacks conventional heroic qualities|Is always the villain|Has supernatural powers
rubric: An anti-hero is the central character of a story who lacks traditional heroic attributes like courage, morality, and idealism.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The Japanese poetic form consisting of three lines with 5-7-5 syllables is _____.
options: Sonnet|Limerick|Haiku|Tanka
rubric: A haiku is a Japanese poem of three unrhymed lines with 5, 7, and 5 syllables respectively, traditionally evoking nature.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The novel 'Season of Migration to the North' was written by _____.
options: Chinua Achebe|Tayeb Salih|Ngugi wa Thiong'o|Ousmane Sembene
rubric: Season of Migration to the North (1966) by Sudanese writer Tayeb Salih is one of the most significant works in Arabic and African literature.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The play 'Trials of Brother Jero' was written by _____.
options: Ola Rotimi|John Pepper Clark|Wole Soyinka|Femi Osofisan
rubric: Trials of Brother Jero (1960) is a satirical comedy by Wole Soyinka about a fraudulent prophet in Lagos.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: What is the unit of measuring electrical current?
options: Volt|Ohm|Ampere|Watt
rubric: Electrical current is measured in Amperes (A). Ohms measure resistance, Volts measure potential difference, and Watts measure power.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The basic unit of life is the _____.
options: Tissue|Organ|Cell|System
rubric: The cell is the smallest and most basic unit of life from which all living organisms are made.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is a metal?
options: Carbon|Sulphur|Copper|Oxygen
rubric: Copper is a metal — it is shiny, conducts electricity and heat, and can be bent without breaking. The others are non-metals.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The ozone layer protects the Earth from _____.
options: Earthquakes|Ultraviolet radiation from the sun|Rainfall|Wind
rubric: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation before it reaches Earth's surface.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Food is digested in the _____.
options: Respiratory system|Circulatory system|Digestive system|Nervous system
rubric: The digestive system (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, intestines) breaks down food into nutrients the body can absorb.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The energy stored in a battery is _____ energy.
options: Kinetic|Chemical|Solar|Nuclear
rubric: A battery stores energy in chemical form, converting it to electrical energy when connected in a circuit.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Plants make their food in the _____.
options: Roots|Stem|Leaves|Flowers
rubric: The leaves are the primary site of photosynthesis in plants — they contain chlorophyll and are adapted to absorb sunlight.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is a property of acids?
options: Turns litmus blue|Tastes bitter|Has pH greater than 7|Turns litmus red
rubric: Acids turn blue litmus paper red, have pH less than 7, taste sour, and react with bases to form salts.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: A simple machine that changes the direction of a force using a rope is a _____.
options: Lever|Pulley|Inclined plane|Gear
rubric: A pulley is a simple machine consisting of a wheel and rope; it changes the direction of the applied force and can reduce effort.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The burning of fossil fuels contributes mainly to _____.
options: Soil erosion|Air pollution and climate change|Water shortage|Noise pollution
rubric: Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) releases CO₂ and other pollutants, contributing to air pollution and the greenhouse effect.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Salt and water are produced when an acid reacts with a _____.
options: Metal|Base|Non-metal|Another acid
rubric: The reaction between an acid and a base (neutralisation) produces a salt and water: acid + base → salt + water.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: An animal that eats both plants and animals is called a _____.
options: Herbivore|Carnivore|Omnivore|Decomposer
rubric: Omnivores consume both plant and animal matter — examples include humans, pigs, and bears.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The force of attraction between objects with mass is called _____.
options: Friction|Gravity|Magnetism|Tension
rubric: Gravity is the universal force of attraction between all objects with mass, described by Newton's law of gravitation.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The organ that produces bile in humans is the _____.
options: Pancreas|Kidney|Stomach|Liver
rubric: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gallbladder and released into the small intestine to aid the digestion of fats.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Rusting is an example of _____.
options: Physical change|Chemical change|Phase change|Reversible change
rubric: Rusting (oxidation of iron) is an irreversible chemical change that alters the chemical composition of iron to form iron oxide.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is NOT a renewable energy source?
options: Solar|Wind|Coal|Hydroelectric
rubric: Coal is a fossil fuel and a non-renewable energy source. Solar, wind, and hydroelectric power are renewable.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The sense organ used for hearing is the _____.
options: Eye|Nose|Ear|Tongue
rubric: The ear is the sensory organ that detects sound waves and transmits them to the brain for interpretation.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Pure water has a pH of _____.
rubric: Pure water is neutral with a pH of exactly 7 at 25°C.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Photosynthesis releases _____ as a by-product.
options: Carbon dioxide|Nitrogen|Oxygen|Hydrogen
rubric: During photosynthesis: CO₂ + H₂O → glucose + O₂. Oxygen is released as a by-product of splitting water molecules.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is a biodegradable waste?
options: Plastic bottles|Food scraps|Glass|Aluminium cans
rubric: Biodegradable waste is broken down naturally by bacteria and other organisms; food scraps decompose, unlike plastics or glass.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: When white light passes through a prism it splits into _____.
options: Two colours|Three colours|A spectrum of seven colours|Infrared and ultraviolet
rubric: White light is split into the visible spectrum (ROYGBIV: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet) when it passes through a glass prism.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The human skeleton has approximately _____ bones.
rubric: The adult human body has 206 bones; babies are born with around 270-300 bones that fuse as they grow.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Oxygen in the air makes up approximately _____ of the atmosphere.
rubric: The Earth's atmosphere is approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other gases including argon and CO₂.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: A magnet always has _____ poles.
options: One|Two|Three|None
rubric: Every magnet has two poles: a North pole and a South pole. These cannot be separated — cutting a magnet produces two smaller magnets each with two poles.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is a function of the skin?
options: Digestion|Excretion of waste and temperature regulation|Hearing|Vision
answer: Excretion of waste and temperature regulation
rubric: The skin excretes waste through sweat glands and regulates body temperature through sweating and changing blood flow to the skin surface.

subject: Integrated Science
