stem: Water purification in treatment plants involves _____.
options: Adding chemicals to make water taste sweet|Filtration, sedimentation, and chlorination|Boiling only|Adding salt
rubric: Water treatment involves sedimentation (settling particles), filtration (removing fine particles), and chlorination (killing bacteria) to make water safe.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Friction is a force that _____.
options: Pulls objects upward|Opposes motion between surfaces in contact|Increases speed|Creates electricity
answer: Opposes motion between surfaces in contact
rubric: Friction is a resistive force that acts between surfaces in contact, opposing relative motion or tendency of motion.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Malaria in humans is caused by _____.
options: Bacteria|A virus|A plasmodium parasite spread by mosquitoes|A fungus
answer: A plasmodium parasite spread by mosquitoes
rubric: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites (a type of protozoan) transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Evaporation is the change from _____.
options: Solid to liquid|Liquid to gas|Gas to liquid|Solid to gas
rubric: Evaporation is the process by which molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough energy to escape into the gas phase.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Noise pollution can cause _____.
options: Better sleep|Hearing impairment|Stronger eyesight|Better memory
rubric: Prolonged exposure to high levels of noise can damage the hair cells in the inner ear, leading to hearing impairment or deafness.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Vaccines help prevent disease by _____.
options: Killing bacteria directly|Training the immune system to recognise pathogens|Replacing damaged cells|Providing nutrients
answer: Training the immune system to recognise pathogens
rubric: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies against a specific pathogen without causing the disease itself.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The instrument used to measure temperature is a _____.
options: Barometer|Thermometer|Hydrometer|Anemometer
rubric: A thermometer is the instrument used to measure temperature in degrees Celsius, Fahrenheit, or Kelvin.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Who was Nigeria's first indigenous Governor-General?
options: Nnamdi Azikiwe|Obafemi Awolowo|Ahmadu Bello|Tafawa Balewa
rubric: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe served as Nigeria's first indigenous Governor-General (1960–1963) and first President (1963–1966).

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Every child has the right to _____.
options: Work in a factory|Own land|Education and protection|Vote in elections
rubric: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child recognises every child's right to education, protection from harm, and access to health care.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The NYSC (National Youth Service Corps) was established to _____.
options: Train soldiers|Promote national unity and development|Manage elections|Collect taxes
rubric: NYSC was established in 1973 to promote national unity by deploying graduates across different states and engaging them in community development.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The arm of government that interprets the law is the _____.
options: Legislature|Executive|Judiciary|Military
rubric: The judiciary (courts and judges) is responsible for interpreting laws, settling disputes, and administering justice.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Which of the following is a sign of good citizenship?
options: Littering public places|Obeying traffic rules|Avoiding taxation|Bribery
rubric: Obeying traffic rules is an example of good citizenship — respecting laws designed to protect public safety and order.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Patriotism means _____.
options: Hating other countries|Love and devotion to one's country|Being a soldier|Paying taxes
answer: Love and devotion to one's country
rubric: Patriotism is love, devotion, and loyalty to one's country and its people, expressed through respect for national symbols and service.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The legislative house at the state level in Nigeria is called the _____.
options: National Assembly|House of Representatives|State House of Assembly|Senate
rubric: Each Nigerian state has a State House of Assembly, which is the state-level unicameral legislature responsible for making state laws.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Discrimination means _____.
options: Treating everyone fairly|Unfair treatment of people based on their identity|Helping the poor|Voting in elections
answer: Unfair treatment of people based on their identity
rubric: Discrimination is the unjust treatment of different categories of people based on race, sex, religion, ethnicity, or other characteristics.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: We can help protect the environment by _____.
options: Cutting down all trees|Disposing of waste properly and recycling|Using more plastic|Burning all rubbish
answer: Disposing of waste properly and recycling
rubric: Proper waste disposal and recycling reduce pollution and the amount of waste sent to landfills, helping protect the natural environment.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Biafran War (Nigerian Civil War) lasted from _____.
rubric: The Nigerian Civil War (Biafran War) was fought from July 1967 to January 1970 following the secession attempt of the Republic of Biafra.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The governor of a state in Nigeria is elected for a term of _____.
options: 2 years|4 years|5 years|6 years
rubric: A Nigerian state governor serves a term of four years and can be re-elected for a maximum of two terms.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Which of the following is an example of helping your community?
options: Stealing from neighbours|Participating in community clean-up exercises|Ignoring your neighbours' needs|Playing all day
rubric: Community service activities like clean-ups promote public health and a sense of collective responsibility for the shared environment.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Nigerian national anthem begins with the words _____.
options: Arise O Compatriots|God Save Nigeria|One Nigeria|Forward Ever
rubric: The Nigerian national anthem begins 'Arise, O Compatriots, Nigeria's call obey...' — adopted in 1978 to replace the first anthem.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The institution responsible for maintaining law and order in Nigeria is the _____.
options: Army|Police|Navy|Air Force
rubric: The Nigeria Police Force (NPF) is the primary agency responsible for maintaining law and order, preventing crime, and protecting citizens.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Freedom of religion means _____.
options: Everyone must practice the same religion|People can worship according to their own belief|Religion is forbidden|Only one religion is allowed
answer: People can worship according to their own belief
rubric: Freedom of religion is the right to hold any religious belief and to practice it without government interference.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Nigeria's first Prime Minister at independence was _____.
options: Nnamdi Azikiwe|Obafemi Awolowo|Abubakar Tafawa Balewa|Ahmadu Bello
rubric: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa became Nigeria's first Prime Minister at independence on 1 October 1960.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Tax money paid to the government is used for _____.
options: Personal use by politicians|Providing public services like roads and schools|Only buying weapons|Foreign travel
answer: Providing public services like roads and schools
rubric: Government tax revenue is used to fund public goods and services including infrastructure, education, healthcare, and security.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Tolerance means _____.
options: Accepting only people from your tribe|Respecting and accepting people with different views and backgrounds|Avoiding all conflict|Being passive
answer: Respecting and accepting people with different views and backgrounds
rubric: Tolerance is the acceptance of others' differences — cultural, religious, or political — without prejudice or discrimination.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Indiscriminate dumping of refuse leads to _____.
options: Better soil quality|Spread of diseases and flooding|More rainfall|Economic growth
rubric: Dumping refuse randomly blocks drainage systems (causing flooding) and provides breeding grounds for disease-carrying organisms.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The term 'democracy' comes from two Greek words meaning _____.
options: King and rule|People and rule|Rich and power|Law and order
rubric: Democracy derives from the Greek words 'demos' (people) and 'kratos' (rule/power) — meaning 'rule by the people'.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Child labour is harmful because it _____.
options: Builds character|Teaches skills|Deprives children of education and health|Makes children responsible
answer: Deprives children of education and health
rubric: Child labour deprives children of their childhood, educational opportunities, and physical and mental development — it is a violation of children's rights.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Federal Capital Territory of Nigeria is _____.
options: Lagos|Ibadan|Abuja|Kano
rubric: Abuja became Nigeria's official Federal Capital Territory in 1991, replacing Lagos as the seat of the federal government.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Respect for elders is important because _____.
options: Elders are always right|Respecting elders is part of our cultural values and promotes social harmony|Only elders can vote|Elders own everything
answer: Respecting elders is part of our cultural values and promotes social harmony
rubric: Respect for elders is a core African cultural value that promotes social cohesion, intergenerational learning, and community harmony.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Nigerian constitution describes Nigeria as a _____.
options: Kingdom|Federal Republic|Empire|Colony
rubric: Nigeria is officially the Federal Republic of Nigeria — a federation of 36 states governed under a republican system.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Unity in diversity means _____.
options: All Nigerians must speak one language|Different ethnic groups working together as one nation|Only one religion is allowed|One state controls others
answer: Different ethnic groups working together as one nation
rubric: Nigeria's national motto, Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress, reflects the value of diverse groups coexisting harmoniously.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Local Government Areas (LGAs) help governance by _____.
options: Taking over federal powers|Bringing government closer to the grassroots|Reducing state powers|Controlling international trade
answer: Bringing government closer to the grassroots
rubric: LGAs are the third tier of government in Nigeria, delivering services like primary health care and sanitation at the community level.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: An eligible citizen who refuses to vote during elections is _____.
options: Breaking the law|Being patriotic|Failing a civic duty|Making a wise choice
rubric: Voting is a fundamental civic responsibility; not voting means failing to participate in shaping leadership and governance.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: A child soldier is a violation of _____.
options: Military rules|Children's rights|National security|Adult rights
rubric: Recruiting children as soldiers violates the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and international humanitarian law.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The groundwork for Nigeria's independence was largely set by the _____.
options: British Army|Colonial legislature and nationalist movements|United Nations|Commonwealth nations
rubric: Nigerian independence in 1960 was the result of decades of agitation by nationalist leaders like Azikiwe, Awolowo, and Balewa within colonial political structures.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Oil spills in the Niger Delta primarily cause _____.
options: Economic growth|Environmental destruction and health problems|Faster crop growth|Improved fishing yields
rubric: Oil spills contaminate soil and water, killing aquatic life and crops, and causing serious health problems for communities.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Public servants are expected to be _____.
options: Loyal to their personal interests|Accountable, impartial, and professional|Only loyal to the ruling party|Absent from work regularly
rubric: Good public service demands accountability (answering for actions), impartiality (treating all citizens equally), and professionalism.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Proper use of public facilities includes _____.
options: Vandalising public property|Reporting faults to the authorities|Writing on public walls|Stealing equipment
rubric: Citizens have a responsibility to maintain and report damage to public facilities to ensure they remain usable by all.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Rule of law ensures that _____.
options: Leaders are above the law|All citizens including leaders are subject to the law|Only the rich have rights|Courts are always right
answer: All citizens including leaders are subject to the law
rubric: Rule of law means no person — however powerful — is above the law; everyone is equally subject to it.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The process by which a bill becomes law includes _____.
options: Approval by the President alone|Debate, passage by legislature, and assent by the executive|Military approval|Approval by traditional rulers
answer: Debate, passage by legislature, and assent by the executive
rubric: A bill passes through readings and debates in the National/State Assembly, is voted on, and then sent to the President/Governor for assent.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded by _____.
options: Uthman dan Fodio|Obafemi Awolowo|Nnamdi Azikiwe|Mungo Park
rubric: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded in 1804 by Uthman dan Fodio following the Fulani jihad in northern Nigeria.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Which of the following helps prevent soil erosion?
options: Cutting down all trees|Planting trees and grasses|Leaving soil exposed|Building on all land
rubric: Tree and grass roots bind soil particles together, preventing them from being washed away by rain (soil erosion).

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: A bill of rights protects citizens against _____.
options: Other countries|Abuse of power by the government|Natural disasters|Economic crises
answer: Abuse of power by the government
rubric: A bill of rights (or constitutional rights chapter) guarantees individual liberties and protects citizens from potential government overreach.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Why is it important to obey traffic laws?
options: To help the police|To reduce accidents and save lives|To drive faster|To pay less fuel
answer: To reduce accidents and save lives
rubric: Traffic laws are designed to regulate movement on roads and prevent collisions, thereby reducing accidents, injuries, and deaths.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The principle of federalism in Nigeria allows _____.
options: One central government to control everything|Different levels of government to share power|Only military governments|States to be completely independent
answer: Different levels of government to share power
rubric: Nigerian federalism distributes powers between federal, state, and local governments, ensuring power is not concentrated in one place.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Which of the following is a violation of human rights?
options: Going to school|Peaceful protest|Torture of prisoners|Freedom of speech
rubric: Torture is a fundamental violation of human rights prohibited under the UN Convention Against Torture and Nigerian law.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Speaker presides over the _____.
options: Senate|House of Representatives|State House of Assembly|Supreme Court
rubric: The Speaker is the presiding officer of the House of Representatives at the federal level; the Senate President presides over the Senate.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The first coup d'état in Nigeria occurred in _____.
rubric: Nigeria's first military coup occurred on 15 January 1966, overthrowing the civilian government of Prime Minister Tafawa Balewa.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Corruption in government leads to _____.
options: Faster development|Underdevelopment and erosion of public trust|Better services|National unity
answer: Underdevelopment and erosion of public trust
rubric: Corruption diverts public resources for private gain, undermining development, weakening institutions, and eroding public trust in government.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Which human activity causes the most water pollution?
options: Farming|Swimming|Industrial waste discharge|Tree planting
rubric: Industrial effluents and chemical waste discharged into rivers and water bodies are a major cause of water pollution.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: National consciousness means _____.
options: Thinking only about one's tribe|Awareness of and pride in being part of a nation|Hatred of other nations|Ignorance of national affairs
answer: Awareness of and pride in being part of a nation
rubric: National consciousness is the sense of belonging to and identifying with one's nation, transcending ethnic or regional identities.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Attorney-General of the Federation is responsible for _____.
options: Collecting taxes|Legal advice to government and prosecution of offences|Making laws|Conducting elections
answer: Legal advice to government and prosecution of offences
rubric: The Attorney-General serves as the chief law officer, providing legal advice to the government and overseeing public prosecutions.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The right to a fair trial includes _____.
options: Being punished before trial|Presumption of innocence until proved guilty|Secret hearings|No right to legal representation
answer: Presumption of innocence until proved guilty
rubric: A fair trial requires that the accused be presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Operation Feed the Nation was launched by _____.
options: Yakubu Gowon|Olusegun Obasanjo|Murtala Mohammed|Shehu Shagari
rubric: Operation Feed the Nation (OFN) was a food-sufficiency programme launched in 1976 by General Olusegun Obasanjo's military government.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Why is census important to Nigeria?
options: It counts only politicians|It helps plan development and allocate resources|It is done for entertainment|It determines oil prices
answer: It helps plan development and allocate resources
rubric: A census provides accurate population data used for planning infrastructure, education, healthcare, and allocating government resources equitably.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Afforestation means _____.
options: Cutting down forests|Planting trees in areas that lacked them|Burning forests|Clearing forests for farming
answer: Planting trees in areas that lacked them
rubric: Afforestation is the establishment of forest in areas where there were none before, helping restore ecosystems and combat climate change.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: A constitution is _____.
options: A type of election|The fundamental law that guides the governance of a country|A government budget|A military decree
answer: The fundamental law that guides the governance of a country
rubric: A constitution is the supreme law of a country, establishing the framework of government and guaranteeing citizens' rights.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: A responsible citizen pays taxes because _____.
options: It is punishable by death not to|Taxes fund public services for everyone|Politicians demand it|It makes you richer
answer: Taxes fund public services for everyone
rubric: Tax revenue pays for public goods and services — roads, hospitals, schools, security — that benefit all members of society.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Aba Women's Riot of 1929 was a protest against _____.
options: Military rule|Colonial taxation policies|Land acquisition|Religious conversion
rubric: The Aba Women's Riot (or Ogu Umunwanyi) was triggered by fears that women would be taxed by the British colonial administration.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Nigeria coat of arms features _____.
options: An eagle and a lion|Two horses (chargers) and a black shield with an eagle|A lion and a buffalo|The Nigerian flag only
answer: Two horses (chargers) and a black shield with an eagle
rubric: Nigeria's coat of arms features a black shield with a silver pall (Y-shape), flanked by two white horses with yellow flowers and an eagle on top.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The Chief of Defence Staff in Nigeria is the overall head of _____.
options: The Police|The Military|The Judiciary|The Civil Service
rubric: The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) is the highest-ranking officer in the Nigerian Armed Forces, coordinating the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Trafficking of persons is a violation of the right to _____.
options: Education|Freedom from slavery and forced labour|Vote|Own property
answer: Freedom from slavery and forced labour
rubric: Human trafficking involves the exploitation of persons through force or coercion for labour or other purposes — a violation of the right to freedom.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Which of the following promotes national development?
options: Bribery and corruption|Hard work, honesty, and innovation|Tribalism|Laziness
rubric: National development is driven by citizens and institutions that value hard work, integrity, and creative problem-solving.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: Immunity in the context of a Nigerian president means _____.
options: He is above the law permanently|He cannot be prosecuted in court while in office|He can imprison anyone|He controls the judiciary
answer: He cannot be prosecuted in court while in office
rubric: Section 308 of the 1999 Constitution grants the President, Vice-President, Governors, and Deputies immunity from civil or criminal proceedings while in office.

subject: Citizenship Education
stem: The River Niger is important to Nigeria because _____.
options: It forms Nigeria's eastern border|It provides water, transport, and is part of the nation's name|It has no significance|It separates Nigeria from Ghana
answer: It provides water, transport, and is part of the nation's name
rubric: The River Niger (and Benue) forms Nigeria's major inland waterway for transport and irrigation; 'Nigeria' is derived from 'River Niger'.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The function of the root hair cells in plants is to _____.
options: Produce food|Absorb water and minerals from the soil|Store food|Support the plant
answer: Absorb water and minerals from the soil
rubric: Root hair cells have a large surface area to efficiently absorb water and dissolved mineral salts from the surrounding soil.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: An echo is produced by _____.
options: Absorption of sound|Reflection of sound|Refraction of light|Diffraction of waves
rubric: An echo occurs when sound waves bounce back from a hard surface and are heard as a repetition of the original sound.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: What state of matter has a definite shape and volume?
options: Gas|Liquid|Solid|Plasma
rubric: Solids have a definite (fixed) shape and volume because their particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement with strong forces between them.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The part of the digestive system where most nutrient absorption occurs is the _____.
options: Stomach|Large intestine|Small intestine|Mouth
rubric: The small intestine is where digested nutrients (sugars, amino acids, fatty acids) are absorbed into the bloodstream through villi.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Oxygen supports burning. This property is called _____.
options: Combustibility|Oxidising support|Supporting combustion|Flammability
rubric: Oxygen itself does not burn but supports and is necessary for combustion — it is a supporter of combustion, not a combustible substance.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The SI unit of length is the _____.
options: Gram|Metre|Litre|Second
rubric: The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length; the second is for time, gram (kilogram) for mass, and litre for volume.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The function of white blood cells is to _____.
options: Carry oxygen|Help blood clot|Fight disease and infection|Transport nutrients
rubric: White blood cells (leucocytes) are part of the immune system, producing antibodies and attacking pathogens.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: A substance that dissolves in water to form a solution is called _____.
options: Insoluble|A solute|A solvent|A mixture
rubric: When a substance (solute) dissolves in a solvent (like water) it forms a solution. Water is the most common solvent.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
options: Carbon dioxide|Methane|Water vapour|Nitrogen
rubric: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, H₂O vapour, N₂O) trap heat in the atmosphere. Nitrogen (N₂) is not a greenhouse gas.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: A wheel and axle is an example of a _____.
options: Chemical reaction|Simple machine|Biological process|Electrical circuit
rubric: A wheel and axle is one of the six classical simple machines, converting rotational force to increase mechanical advantage.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Phototropism is the growth of a plant in response to _____.
options: Water|Gravity|Light|Touch
rubric: Phototropism is the directional growth of plants in response to light — stems grow toward light (positive phototropism).

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The process of separating salt from sea water by heating is called _____.
options: Filtration|Distillation|Evaporation|Decanting
rubric: To obtain salt from sea water, the water is evaporated (the sea water is heated until the water turns to steam, leaving salt behind).

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is the correct unit for speed?
options: Kg|m/s|Newton|Joule
rubric: Speed is measured in metres per second (m/s) — distance divided by time.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The process by which organisms reproduce by producing offspring similar to themselves is called _____.
options: Photosynthesis|Reproduction|Digestion|Respiration
rubric: Reproduction is the biological process by which new individual organisms are produced from their parents.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Iron + oxygen → iron oxide is an example of _____.
options: Reduction|Oxidation|Decomposition|Displacement
rubric: Iron reacting with oxygen to form iron oxide (rust) is an oxidation reaction — oxygen is added to the substance.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: An electric circuit must be _____ for current to flow.
options: Open|Broken|Complete (closed)|Isolated
rubric: Electric current flows only in a complete (closed) circuit — one with no gaps or breaks from source through conductor back to source.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is an example of a vertebrate?
options: Earthworm|Butterfly|Dog|Cockroach
rubric: Vertebrates have a backbone (vertebral column). Among the options, only the dog is a vertebrate; the others are invertebrates.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Excessive use of fertilisers can cause _____.
options: Better crop yields always|Soil and water pollution|Reduced pests|Faster plant growth always
rubric: Overuse of chemical fertilisers can lead to nutrient runoff into waterways (eutrophication) and soil acidification and degradation.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Shadows are formed because light _____.
options: Travels in curved paths|Cannot pass through all objects|Has colour|Moves slowly
rubric: Shadows form when opaque objects block light from passing through, creating a dark area on the other side.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: A mixture differs from a compound because in a mixture _____.
options: Elements are chemically bonded|Components can be separated by physical means|A new substance is formed|The composition is fixed
answer: Components can be separated by physical means
rubric: In a mixture, components retain their properties and can be separated physically (by filtering, evaporation, etc.); compounds require chemical processes.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The correct sequence in a food chain is _____.
options: Consumer → Producer → Decomposer|Producer → Primary consumer → Secondary consumer|Decomposer → Consumer → Producer|Secondary consumer → Primary consumer → Producer
rubric: Energy flows from producers (plants) to primary consumers (herbivores) to secondary consumers (carnivores) in a food chain.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Day and night are caused by _____.
options: The moon blocking the sun|Earth rotating on its axis|Earth revolving round the sun|The sun moving around Earth
rubric: Day and night result from Earth spinning on its own axis every 24 hours, with different parts facing toward or away from the sun.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: Which of the following is the universal solvent?
options: Oil|Alcohol|Water|Vinegar
rubric: Water is called the universal solvent because it can dissolve more substances than any other liquid due to its polarity.

subject: Integrated Science
stem: The vitamin that prevents scurvy is _____.
options: Vitamin A|Vitamin B|Vitamin C|Vitamin D

options: Receipts from abroad exceed payments to abroad|Imports exceed exports|The country owes more money|Foreign currency reserves are falling
answer: Receipts from abroad exceed payments to abroad
rubric: A favourable (positive/surplus) balance of payments means total foreign exchange receipts (exports + capital inflows) exceed total payments (imports + capital outflows).

subject: Economics
stem: An expansionary fiscal policy involves
options: Increasing government spending and/or reducing taxes|Raising taxes and reducing spending|Increasing interest rates|Reducing money supply
answer: Increasing government spending and/or reducing taxes
rubric: Expansionary fiscal policy stimulates the economy by increasing government expenditure and/or cutting taxes to boost aggregate demand and employment.

subject: Economics
stem: The main purpose of a government budget is to
options: Plan government revenues and expenditures for the year|Fix exchange rates|Determine interest rates|Set import tariffs
answer: Plan government revenues and expenditures for the year
rubric: A government budget is an annual financial statement that outlines expected revenues and planned expenditures
predicted: used as a fiscal policy tool to manage the economy.

subject: Economics
stem: Population census is important for economic planning because it
options: Provides data on population size and distribution for planning|Determines immigration policy|Sets labour market wages|Controls population growth
answer: Provides data on population size and distribution for planning
rubric: Population census provides vital data on population size
column12: and growth rates essential for government planning of schools

subject: Economics
stem: Subsistence farming is characterized by
options: Producing mainly for the farmer's own consumption|Producing for export markets|Use of modern machinery|High commercial output
answer: Producing mainly for the farmer's own consumption
rubric: Subsistence farming involves growing crops and rearing animals primarily to feed the farmer's family rather than for commercial sale. Surplus (if any) may be sold.

subject: Economics
stem: The supply of labour depends on
options: Population size, working age, and participation rates|Only the wage rate|Government policy alone|Number of factories
answer: Population size, working age, and participation rates
rubric: Labour supply depends on the working-age population
column12: migration
column13: and social factors like female participation in the workforce.

subject: Economics
stem: Average fixed cost (AFC) as output increases will
options: Continuously fall|Continuously rise|Remain constant|First fall then rise
rubric: Average Fixed Cost = Total Fixed Cost / Output. As output increases
predicted: the same fixed cost is spread over more units

subject: Economics
stem: Economic development differs from economic growth in that development involves
options: Qualitative improvements in living standards alongside quantitative growth|Only an increase in GDP|Just industrial expansion|A fall in inflation
answer: Qualitative improvements in living standards alongside quantitative growth
rubric: Economic development is a broader concept that includes GDP growth PLUS improvements in quality of life
column12: education

subject: Economics
stem: Cost-push inflation is caused by
options: Rising production costs being passed to consumers as higher prices|Excess money in the economy|Increased consumer spending|Government budget surplus
answer: Rising production costs being passed to consumers as higher prices
rubric: Cost-push inflation occurs when production costs (wages
column12: causing firms to increase their prices — pushing inflation from the supply side.

subject: Economics
stem: Giffen goods are inferior goods for which
options: Demand rises as price rises|Demand falls as price rises|Supply increases with price|Demand is perfectly inelastic
rubric: Giffen goods are a special case of inferior goods where, despite a price rise, demand increases because the income effect (reduced purchasing power) outweighs the substitution effect.

subject: Economics
stem: Perfect competition is characterized by
options: Homogeneous products and price-taking firms|Product differentiation|Few sellers|Price-setting by firms
rubric: In perfect competition
column11: are price-takers (no individual firm influences market price)
column12: and there is free entry and exit.

subject: Economics
stem: A mixed economy is one in which
options: Both private and government sectors coexist and participate in production|Only the government controls all production|All resources are privately owned|There is no government intervention
answer: Both private and government sectors coexist and participate in production
rubric: A mixed economy combines features of market (private sector) and command (government-controlled) economies — most modern economies are of this type.

subject: Economics
stem: Fixed costs are costs that
options: Do not change with the level of output|Increase as production rises|Are always variable|Decrease as output increases
answer: Do not change with the level of output
rubric: Fixed costs (e.g.
column12: machinery depreciation) remain constant regardless of how much or how little output a firm produces in the short run.

subject: Economics
stem: The instrument used by the central bank to increase money supply is
options: Lowering cash reserve ratio|Raising minimum lending rate|Increasing taxes|Reducing government spending
rubric: When the central bank lowers the cash reserve ratio (CRR)
predicted: commercial banks can lend a higher proportion of their deposits

subject: Economics
stem: Structural unemployment occurs when
options: Workers' skills do not match available jobs due to economic change|There is seasonal reduction in work|Workers are between jobs|Wages are too low to attract workers
answer: Workers' skills do not match available jobs due to economic change
rubric: Structural unemployment results from a mismatch between workers' skills and the requirements of available jobs — often caused by technological change or industrial decline.

subject: Economics
stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) measures
options: Life expectancy, education, and per-capita income|Only GDP per capita|Military strength|Natural resource wealth
answer: Life expectancy, education, and per-capita income
rubric: The HDI combines three dimensions: life expectancy (health)
column11: and GNI per capita (standard of living) to measure human development.

subject: Economics
stem: Land tenure refers to
options: The system by which land is owned and used|The fertility of soil|Crop rotation practices|The taxation of land
answer: The system by which land is owned and used
rubric: Land tenure is the relationship (legally or customarily defined) between people with respect to land — it defines who can use land

subject: Literature in English
stem: A soliloquy in drama is
options: A speech delivered by a character alone on stage|A dialogue between two characters|A choral song|An extended metaphor in poetry
answer: A speech delivered by a character alone on stage
rubric: A soliloquy is a dramatic device where a character speaks their thoughts aloud to the audience while alone on stage — revealing inner feelings not shared with other characters.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The climax of a play is
options: The point of highest dramatic tension|The opening scene|The final scene|The subplot resolution
answer: The point of highest dramatic tension
rubric: The climax is the moment of highest tension or excitement in a drama — the turning point after which the action moves toward resolution.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Personification is a literary device that
options: Gives human qualities to non-human things|Compares two unlike things using 'like' or 'as'|Repeats initial consonant sounds|Exaggerates for effect
answer: Gives human qualities to non-human things
rubric: Personification is a figure of speech that attributes human characteristics
column12: objects

subject: Literature in English
stem: The rhyme scheme of a Shakespearean sonnet ends with
options: A rhyming couplet|A sestet|An octave|Free verse
rubric: A Shakespearean (Elizabethan) sonnet has 14 lines divided into three quatrains (ABAB CDCD EFEF) followed by a concluding rhyming couplet (GG).

subject: Literature in English
stem: First-person narration uses which pronoun throughout?
options: I|He|She|They
rubric: First-person narrative uses 'I' (the narrator) to tell the story, placing the reader inside the narrator's perspective — as opposed to third-person ('he', 'she', 'they').

subject: Literature in English
stem: Stream of consciousness is a narrative technique that
options: Records a character's continuous flow of thoughts|Describes physical action only|Uses dialogue to advance plot|Tells events in chronological order
answer: Records a character's continuous flow of thoughts
rubric: Stream of consciousness is a narrative method that depicts the continuous
predicted: unedited flow of thoughts and feelings of a character's mind.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An oxymoron is a figure of speech that
options: Combines two contradictory terms|Repeats words at the beginning of lines|Compares using 'like' or 'as'|Uses understatement for effect
rubric: An oxymoron combines two seemingly contradictory terms to create a paradoxical effect, e.g., 'deafening silence', 'living death', 'bitter sweet'.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Dramatic irony occurs when
options: The audience knows something characters do not|Two characters misunderstand each other|The author directly addresses the reader|Events are the opposite of what is expected
answer: The audience knows something characters do not
rubric: Dramatic irony is a literary technique where the audience/reader has more knowledge about what is happening than the characters in the story themselves.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Iambic pentameter refers to a line of poetry with
options: Five iambic feet (ten syllables)|Four feet|Six feet|Stressed syllables only
rubric: Iambic pentameter consists of five iambs per line, where each iamb is an unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable — ten syllables total. Shakespeare used this extensively.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A tragic flaw (hamartia) is
options: A character's error or weakness leading to their downfall|A comic element in tragedy|A flaw in the plot structure|An imperfect metaphor
answer: A character's error or weakness leading to their downfall
rubric: Hamartia (from Aristotle's Poetics) is the tragic hero's fatal flaw or error in judgment that causes their eventual downfall — e.g., Okonkwo's inflexibility in "Things Fall Apart".

subject: Literature in English
stem: The denouement of a story is
options: The resolution and untying of the plot after the climax|The central conflict|The narrative technique|The opening exposition
answer: The resolution and untying of the plot after the climax
rubric: The denouement (French for 'unknotting') is the final part of a story following the climax — where conflicts are resolved, loose ends are tied, and the outcome is revealed.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Chinua Achebe's novel 'Things Fall Apart' deals primarily with
options: The impact of colonialism on Igbo society|Nigerian independence|The Biafran war|Economic development
answer: The impact of colonialism on Igbo society
rubric: Achebe's "Things Fall Apart" (1958) portrays the clash between Igbo traditional culture and the disruption caused by European colonialism and Christian missionaries.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An elegy is a poem written to
options: Mourn or lament the death of someone|Celebrate a happy occasion|Praise a hero's deeds|Describe nature
answer: Mourn or lament the death of someone
rubric: An elegy is a mournful, reflective poem typically written as a lament for the death of a person, often meditating on loss, grief, and sometimes hope.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Wole Soyinka is best known as a Nigerian
options: Playwright and poet|Novelist only|Short story writer|Music composer
rubric: Wole Soyinka is Nigeria's foremost playwright and poet — his major works include "Death and the King's Horseman", "The Lion and the Jewel", and "A Dance of the Forests". He won the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Enjambment in poetry refers to
options: Continuation of a sentence beyond the end of a line|A pause at the end of a line|Repetition of vowel sounds|Rhyme within a line
answer: Continuation of a sentence beyond the end of a line
rubric: Enjambment (from French 'to straddle') is the continuation of a grammatical sentence or phrase from one line of poetry to the next without a terminal punctuation mark.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An omniscient narrator
options: Knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters|Only tells one character's story|Is a character in the story|Only describes external events
answer: Knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters
rubric: An omniscient (all-knowing) narrator has complete knowledge of all characters' inner thoughts
column11: and events — giving the author maximum freedom to tell the story.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Alliteration is the repetition of
options: Initial consonant sounds in nearby words|Vowel sounds|End rhymes|A refrain in poetry
answer: Initial consonant sounds in nearby words
rubric: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in consecutive or closely associated words — e.g., "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."

subject: Literature in English
stem: A farce is a type of comedy that relies on
options: Exaggerated and improbable situations for humour|Subtle social commentary|Tragic events|Complex philosophical themes
answer: Exaggerated and improbable situations for humour
rubric: A farce is a comedy that depends on improbable situations, physical humor (slapstick), mistaken identities, and rapid, exaggerated events to provoke laughter.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In poetry, a stanza is
options: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem|A single line of verse|The theme of a poem|The rhythm pattern
answer: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem
rubric: A stanza is a grouped set of lines within a poem — similar to a paragraph in prose. Stanzas can be couplets (2 lines), quatrains (4 lines), sestets (6 lines), and so on.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Ngugi wa Thiong'o is a celebrated writer from
options: Kenya|Nigeria|Ghana|South Africa
rubric: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o is one of Africa's foremost authors, born in Kenya. Notable works include "Weep Not, Child", "A Grain of Wheat", and "Petals of Blood".

subject: Literature in English
stem: A bildungsroman is a novel that
options: Traces the psychological and moral growth of the protagonist|Focuses on war narratives|Describes supernatural events|Is written in verse form
answer: Traces the psychological and moral growth of the protagonist
rubric: A bildungsroman (German: 'novel of education') follows the coming-of-age and development of a young protagonist from youth to maturity — e.g., "Jane Eyre" or "Great Expectations".

subject: Literature in English
stem: The term 'aside' in drama refers to
options: Words spoken to the audience but not heard by other characters|A long monologue|A stage direction|A song between scenes
answer: Words spoken to the audience but not heard by other characters
rubric: An 'aside' is a brief dramatic device where a character speaks directly to the audience with remarks that other characters on stage cannot hear.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Irony involves
options: Saying the opposite of what is meant|Comparing two unlike things|Repeating the same word|Describing sounds with words
answer: Saying the opposite of what is meant
rubric: Verbal irony involves saying the opposite of what is literally meant for effect — e.g., saying "Oh, great!" when something goes wrong. It can also encompass situational and dramatic irony.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Onomatopoeia is the use of words
options: Whose sound imitates the sound they describe|That create visual images|That compare using 'as'|That address an absent person
answer: Whose sound imitates the sound they describe
rubric: Onomatopoeia is a figure of speech where the word phonetically mimics the sound it describes — e.g., 'buzz', 'crash', 'hiss', 'sizzle', 'murmur'.

subject: Biology
stem: The powerhouse of the cell is the
options: Mitochondrion|Nucleus|Ribosome|Cell membrane
rubric: The mitochondrion is called the powerhouse of the cell because it produces ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through cellular respiration — providing energy for cell activities.

subject: Biology
stem: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
options: Ribosome|Lysosome|Vacuole|Golgi apparatus
rubric: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis. They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences into amino acid chains to build proteins.

subject: Biology
stem: The scientific study of heredity and variation is called
options: Genetics|Ecology|Physiology|Taxonomy
rubric: Genetics is the branch of biology that deals with the study of genes
predicted: heredity (how traits are passed from parents to offspring)

subject: Biology
stem: In genetics, dominant alleles
options: Mask the expression of recessive alleles|Are always passed to offspring|Cause genetic disorders|Are found only in homozygotes
answer: Mask the expression of recessive alleles
rubric: A dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy is present (heterozygous condition)
predicted: masking the effect of the recessive allele.

subject: Biology
stem: A food chain always begins with
options: A producer (green plant)|A primary consumer|A decomposer|A carnivore
rubric: Food chains always start with producers (autotrophs) — green plants that convert sunlight energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: Decomposers in an ecosystem primarily function to
options: Break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients|Produce food through photosynthesis|Consume primary producers|Regulate population size
answer: Break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients
rubric: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic material into simpler inorganic compounds that are returned to the soil and reused by plants.

subject: Biology
stem: The largest organ in the human body is
options: The skin|The liver|The brain|The lung
rubric: The skin is the largest organ of the human body. In adults it covers approximately 1.5–2 square metres and constitutes about 15% of total body weight.

subject: Biology
stem: The function of the kidney is to
options: Filter blood and excrete metabolic waste as urine|Produce bile|Pump blood|Digest food
answer: Filter blood and excrete metabolic waste as urine
rubric: The kidneys filter the blood to remove waste products (especially urea from protein metabolism) and excess water

subject: Biology
stem: Photosynthesis takes place mainly in the
options: Chloroplasts of leaf cells|Mitochondria|Roots|Stem bark
rubric: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts
predicted: particularly in the mesophyll cells of leaves
column11: where chlorophyll absorbs light energy to convert CO₂ and H₂O into glucose.

subject: Biology
stem: The process by which plants lose water through their leaves is called
options: Transpiration|Photosynthesis|Osmosis|Respiration
rubric: Transpiration is the process by which water absorbed by plant roots moves up through the plant and evaporates from leaves through pores called stomata.

subject: Biology
stem: Charles Darwin's theory of evolution is based on
options: Natural selection — survival of the fittest|Inheritance of acquired characteristics|Spontaneous generation|Directed mutation
answer: Natural selection — survival of the fittest
rubric: Darwin's theory of natural selection states that organisms with advantageous traits survive and reproduce more successfully ('survival of the fittest'), passing traits to offspring.

subject: Biology
stem: Fertilization in humans occurs in the
options: Fallopian tube (oviduct)|Uterus|Ovary|Vagina
rubric: Fertilization — the union of sperm and egg — normally occurs in the fallopian tube (oviduct). The fertilized egg then travels to the uterus for implantation.

subject: Biology
stem: The enzyme pepsin in the stomach is responsible for
options: Digesting proteins|Digesting carbohydrates|Digesting fats|Absorbing vitamins
rubric: Pepsin is a protease enzyme found in the stomach that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides. It is produced as inactive pepsinogen, activated by stomach acid (HCl).

subject: Biology
stem: A person with blood group O has the genotype
options: ii|IA IB|IA i|IB i
rubric: In the ABO blood group system, blood group O has genotype ii (homozygous recessive) — the person inherits the recessive i allele from both parents.

subject: Biology
stem: The relationship between a lion and a zebra in an ecosystem is
options: Predation|Mutualism|Commensalism|Parasitism
rubric: Predation is a relationship where one organism (predator — the lion) kills and feeds on another organism (prey — the zebra). Both populations influence each other's size.

subject: Biology
stem: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from
options: A region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration through a semi-permeable membrane|Lower to higher concentration|High pressure to low pressure|Inside to outside only
answer: A region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration through a semi-permeable membrane
rubric: Osmosis is the passive movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane from a dilute solution (higher water concentration) to a concentrated solution.

subject: Biology
stem: The part of the brain that controls balance and coordination is the
options: Cerebellum|Cerebrum|Medulla oblongata|Hypothalamus
rubric: The cerebellum ('little brain') is located at the back of the brain and coordinates voluntary movements, posture, and balance. Damage leads to ataxia.

subject: Biology
stem: The term 'niche' in ecology refers to
options: The role and position of an organism in its ecosystem|The physical location of an organism|The food an organism eats|The size of a population
answer: The role and position of an organism in its ecosystem
rubric: An organism's ecological niche encompasses its role in the ecosystem — including its habitat
column12: and interactions with other species.

subject: Biology
stem: Xylem tissue in plants is responsible for
options: Transporting water and mineral salts from roots to leaves|Transporting sugars from leaves to other parts|Supporting the plant only|Absorbing sunlight
answer: Transporting water and mineral salts from roots to leaves
rubric: Xylem is the vascular tissue that conducts water and dissolved minerals from the roots upward through the stem to the leaves (transpiration stream).

subject: Biology
stem: The hormone insulin is produced by the
options: Pancreas|Liver|Adrenal glands|Thyroid gland
rubric: Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. It regulates blood glucose by enabling cells to absorb glucose — deficiency causes diabetes.

subject: Biology
stem: Asexual reproduction results in offspring that are
options: Genetically identical to the parent|Genetically diverse|Produced by fertilization|Dependent on both parents
rubric: Asexual reproduction (e.g., budding, fragmentation, binary fission) produces offspring that are genetically identical to the parent — they are clones, as no genetic recombination occurs.

subject: Biology
stem: Fossils provide evidence for evolution by
options: Showing physical remains of organisms from different geological periods|Proving spontaneous generation|Demonstrating acquired characteristics|Disproving natural selection
answer: Showing physical remains of organisms from different geological periods
rubric: Fossils are preserved remains of organisms from past geological periods. The fossil record shows progressive changes in organisms over time — supporting the theory of evolution.

subject: Biology
stem: Active transport differs from diffusion in that active transport
options: Requires energy (ATP) to move substances against a concentration gradient|Moves substances from high to low concentration|Requires no energy|Occurs only in plants
answer: Requires energy (ATP) to move substances against a concentration gradient
rubric: Active transport uses energy (ATP) to move molecules against their concentration gradient (from low to high concentration) — unlike diffusion which is passive.

subject: Biology
stem: The function of the alveoli in the lungs is to
options: Provide a large surface area for gas exchange|Produce mucus|Filter blood|Pump air into the lungs
answer: Provide a large surface area for gas exchange
rubric: Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs with thin walls and rich blood supply that provide a large surface area (about 70m²) for efficient exchange of O₂ and CO₂.

subject: Physics
stem: The unit of force in the SI system is the
options: Newton|Joule|Watt|Pascal
rubric: The Newton (N) is the SI unit of force. 1 Newton is the force needed to accelerate a mass of 1 kg at 1 m/s² — named after Isaac Newton.

subject: Physics
stem: Newton's third law of motion states that
options: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction|A body remains at rest unless acted upon by a force|Force equals mass times acceleration|Momentum is always conserved
answer: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
rubric: Newton's Third Law: when object A exerts a force on object B, object B exerts an equal and opposite force on object A — action and reaction forces.

subject: Physics
stem: The frequency of a wave is the number of
options: Complete oscillations per second|Wavelengths per minute|Metres per second|Cycles per hour
rubric: Frequency is the number of complete wave cycles (oscillations) that occur per second. It is measured in Hertz (Hz) where 1 Hz = 1 cycle per second.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following is a transverse wave?
options: Light waves|Sound waves|Compression waves in air|P-waves in an earthquake
rubric: Light (electromagnetic radiation) is a transverse wave — the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy travel. Sound is a longitudinal (compression) wave.

subject: Physics
stem: Ohm's Law states that
options: Current through a conductor is proportional to voltage across it at constant temperature|Voltage equals power times resistance|Current is always constant|Resistance decreases with temperature
answer: Current through a conductor is proportional to voltage across it at constant temperature
rubric: Ohm's Law: V = IR, meaning the current (I) through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) across it, provided temperature is constant.

subject: Physics
stem: In a series circuit, the total resistance is
options: The sum of all individual resistances|The average of resistances|Less than the smallest resistance|Equal to any one resistance
answer: The sum of all individual resistances
rubric: In a series circuit, total resistance R_total = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + …. All current must pass through each resistor in turn, so resistances add up.

subject: Physics
stem: Work done is calculated as
options: Force multiplied by distance in the direction of the force|Force divided by distance|Mass times velocity|Energy divided by time
answer: Force multiplied by distance in the direction of the force
rubric: Work done (W) = Force (F) × distance (d) × cos θ, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement. Work is measured in Joules (J).

subject: Physics
stem: The kinetic energy of a moving object depends on its
options: Mass and velocity|Weight only|Volume only|Shape only
rubric: Kinetic Energy (KE) = ½mv², where m is mass and v is velocity. KE increases with the square of velocity — doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy.

subject: Physics
stem: The specific heat capacity of a substance is
options: The amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg by 1°C|The total heat content|The rate of heat transfer|The heat needed to change state
answer: The amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg by 1°C
rubric: Specific heat capacity (c) is the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1°C (or 1 K). Formula: Q = mcΔT.

subject: Physics
stem: Latent heat is the heat energy absorbed or released
options: During a change of state without temperature change|When heating a gas|When compressing a liquid|When mixing two substances
answer: During a change of state without temperature change
rubric: Latent heat is the energy absorbed or released during a phase change (melting, boiling, condensation, freezing) at constant temperature — e.g., water to steam at 100°C.

subject: Physics
stem: A concave mirror
options: Converges reflected light rays to a focus|Diverges reflected light rays|Is the back of a spoon|Has no focal point
answer: Converges reflected light rays to a focus
rubric: A concave (converging) mirror has a reflecting surface that curves inward. Parallel rays hitting it are reflected and converge at the focal point — used in torches, telescopes.

subject: Physics
stem: Total internal reflection occurs when
options: Light travels from a denser to a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle|Light passes through a prism|Light is reflected off a plane mirror|Light enters water at 90°
answer: Light travels from a denser to a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
rubric: TIR occurs when light in a denser medium hits the boundary at an angle exceeding the critical angle — it is completely reflected back. This is the principle behind optical fibres.

subject: Physics
stem: Electromagnetic induction is the production of
options: An electromotive force (EMF) in a conductor by a changing magnetic field|Electric current in a static conductor|Magnetic field by a battery|Heat by resistance
answer: An electromotive force (EMF) in a conductor by a changing magnetic field
rubric: Faraday's Law: electromagnetic induction is the generation of an EMF (and hence current) in a conductor when it is exposed to a changing magnetic field — basis of generators.

subject: Physics
stem: A step-up transformer
options: Increases voltage and decreases current|Decreases voltage and increases current|Increases both voltage and current|Decreases both voltage and current
rubric: A step-up transformer increases the output voltage (more turns in secondary coil). Since power is conserved (P=VI), the current decreases proportionally.

subject: Physics
stem: Radioactivity involves the emission of radiation from
options: Unstable nuclei of atoms|Stable electron shells|Magnetic fields|Chemical bonds
rubric: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation (alpha, beta, or gamma) from the unstable nucleus of an atom as it seeks a more stable configuration.

subject: Physics
stem: The half-life of a radioactive substance is
options: The time for half its atoms to decay|The time to fully decay|Half the atomic mass|Half the emission rate
answer: The time for half its atoms to decay
rubric: Half-life (t₁/₂) is the time required for exactly half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay. After one half-life, 50% remain; after two, 25% remain, etc.

subject: Physics
stem: Pressure is defined as
options: Force per unit area|Force times area|Mass per unit volume|Weight per unit mass
rubric: Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A). It is measured in Pascals (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Pressure increases as area decreases for the same applied force.

subject: Physics
stem: The SI unit of power is the
options: Watt|Joule|Newton|Pascal
rubric: Power (P) = Work Done / Time = Energy / Time. The SI unit is the Watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s — named after James Watt.

subject: Physics
stem: Archimedes' principle states that
options: The upward buoyant force on a submerged object equals the weight of fluid displaced|Objects sink in all fluids|Pressure increases with depth|Density equals mass times volume
answer: The upward buoyant force on a submerged object equals the weight of fluid displaced
rubric: Archimedes' Principle: a body submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces — explaining why ships float.

subject: Physics
stem: Surface tension is
options: The elastic-like tendency of liquid surfaces to contract|The viscosity of a liquid|The pressure at the bottom of a liquid|The boiling point of a liquid
answer: The elastic-like tendency of liquid surfaces to contract
rubric: Surface tension is the tendency of liquid surfaces to contract due to cohesive forces between molecules — allowing water striders to walk on water.

subject: Physics
stem: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is approximately
rubric: The speed of sound in air at room temperature (~20°C) is approximately 343 m/s. It is much faster in liquids and solids, and much slower than the speed of light.

subject: Physics
stem: Centripetal acceleration is directed
options: Towards the centre of the circular path|Away from the centre|Tangent to the circular path|Upward
answer: Towards the centre of the circular path
rubric: Centripetal acceleration (a = v²/r) is always directed toward the centre of the circular path. The centripetal force causing it also points inward (centre-seeking).

subject: Physics
stem: A capacitor stores energy in
options: An electric field|A magnetic field|Chemical bonds|Mechanical compression
rubric: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the electric field between its plates. Capacitance C = Q/V, measured in Farads. It charges and discharges rapidly.

subject: Physics
stem: The photoelectric effect was explained by
options: Albert Einstein using the concept of photons|Isaac Newton using wave theory|Niels Bohr using orbital theory|James Maxwell using electromagnetic theory
answer: Albert Einstein using the concept of photons
rubric: Einstein explained the photoelectric effect (1905) by proposing that light consists of discrete packets of energy called photons (E = hf). This work earned him the 1921 Nobel Prize.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The atomic number of an element is equal to
options: The number of protons in the nucleus|The number of neutrons|The mass number|The number of electron shells
answer: The number of protons in the nucleus
rubric: The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus. It uniquely identifies the element and in a neutral atom equals the number of electrons.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with
options: The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons|Different numbers of protons|Different electron configurations|The same mass number
answer: The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
rubric: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same proton number) that have different numbers of neutrons — giving different mass numbers. E.g., carbon-12 and carbon-14.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An ionic bond forms when
options: One atom transfers electrons to another|Atoms share electrons equally|Electrons are shared unequally|Metals bond with metals
answer: One atom transfers electrons to another
rubric: An ionic bond results from the electrostatic attraction between a positive ion (cation) and a negative ion (anion) formed when one atom transfers electron(s) to another — typically metal + non-metal.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A covalent bond is formed by
options: Sharing of electrons between two non-metal atoms|Transfer of electrons|Attraction between ions|Metallic bonding
answer: Sharing of electrons between two non-metal atoms
rubric: A covalent bond forms when two non-metal atoms share one or more pairs of electrons. Both atoms contribute electrons to the shared pair — e.g., H₂, H₂O, CO₂.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An acid is a substance that
options: Donates a proton (H⁺) to another substance|Accepts a proton|Has a pH above 7|Turns litmus blue
answer: Donates a proton (H⁺) to another substance
rubric: According to Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is a proton (H⁺) donor. In water, acids release H⁺ ions — e.g., HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The pH of pure water at 25°C is
rubric: Pure water is neutral with a pH of 7 at 25°C. Solutions with pH < 7 are acidic; pH > 7 are alkaline/basic.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The homologous series with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ is
options: Alkanes|Alkenes|Alkynes|Alcohols
rubric: Alkanes have the general molecular formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. They are saturated hydrocarbons — e.g., methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), propane (C₃H₈).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Ethanol is produced commercially by the fermentation of
options: Sugars by yeast|Crude oil|Coal|Cellulose
rubric: Industrial ethanol is produced by fermentation: yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) converts sugars (glucose/sucrose) to ethanol and CO₂ under anaerobic conditions.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³) represents
options: The number of particles in one mole of a substance|The mass of one molecule|The volume of one mole of gas|The atomic mass unit
answer: The number of particles in one mole of a substance
rubric: Avogadro's constant (Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹) is the number of atoms, molecules, or ions in one mole of any substance — fundamental to quantitative chemistry.

subject: Chemistry
stem: During electrolysis, reduction occurs at the
options: Cathode (negative electrode)|Anode (positive electrode)|Electrolyte|External circuit
rubric: At the cathode in electrolysis, positive ions (cations) gain electrons — they are reduced: e.g., Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Oxidation occurs at the anode.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by
options: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy|Increasing temperature|Adding more reactants|Reducing products
answer: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
rubric: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy. The catalyst is not consumed in the overall reaction.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have
options: The same number of outer shell electrons|The same atomic mass|The same number of neutrons|Equal electronegativity
answer: The same number of outer shell electrons
rubric: Elements in the same group (vertical column) of the periodic table have the same number of valence (outer shell) electrons — giving them similar chemical properties.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In a redox reaction, oxidation involves
options: Loss of electrons|Gain of electrons|Loss of protons|Gain of oxygen ions
rubric: Oxidation = Loss of electrons (OIL — Oxidation Is Loss). In a redox reaction, one substance is oxidized (loses electrons) while another is reduced (gains electrons).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Le Chatelier's principle states that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it will
options: Shift to counteract the disturbance and re-establish equilibrium|Collapse completely|Increase all concentrations|Produce only more products
answer: Shift to counteract the disturbance and re-establish equilibrium
rubric: Le Chatelier's Principle: a system at equilibrium will respond to a stress (change in concentration, pressure, or temperature) by shifting position to minimize the effect.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Saponification is the process used to manufacture
options: Soap from fats and alkali|Plastics from monomers|Fertilizers from nitrogen|Petrol from crude oil
rubric: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats (triglycerides) with a strong base (NaOH or KOH) to produce glycerol and fatty acid salts (soap).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron and
options: "Chromium and nickel|Carbon only|Aluminium|Copper"
rubric: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium (at least 10.5%) and usually nickel. The chromium forms a passive oxide layer that resists corrosion.

subject: Chemistry
stem: At STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure), one mole of an ideal gas occupies
options: 22.4 litres|1 litre|44.8 litres|11.2 litres
rubric: At STP (0°C and 1 atm), one mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 litres (22.4 dm³) — the molar volume of an ideal gas at standard conditions.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The process of extracting aluminium from aluminium oxide by electrolysis is called
options: The Hall-Héroult process|The Haber process|The Frasch process|The Solvay process
rubric: The Hall-Héroult process is used to extract aluminium by electrolysing molten aluminium oxide (dissolved in cryolite) at high temperature.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Addition polymerization involves
options: Many monomer molecules joining together without any byproduct|Condensation of monomers with loss of water|Breaking of polymers into monomers|Reaction of different monomers
answer: Many monomer molecules joining together without any byproduct
rubric: Addition polymerization occurs when many unsaturated monomer molecules join together through opening of double bonds — e.g., ethene polymerizes to form poly(ethene).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following exhibits hydrogen bonding?
options: Water (H₂O)|Methane (CH₄)|Carbon dioxide (CO₂)|Nitrogen gas (N₂)
rubric: Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom (N, O, F). In water, O-H…O hydrogen bonds give water its unusually high boiling point.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A buffer solution resists changes in pH because it contains
options: A weak acid and its conjugate base (or a weak base and its conjugate acid)|A strong acid only|Excess alkali|Pure water
answer: A weak acid and its conjugate base (or a weak base and its conjugate acid)
rubric: A buffer contains a weak acid/base and its conjugate salt. When H⁺ or OH⁻ is added, the weak acid/base neutralizes it — maintaining nearly constant pH.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A flame test showing a brick-red colour indicates the presence of
options: Calcium ions (Ca²⁺)|Sodium ions (Na⁺)|Potassium ions (K⁺)|Copper ions (Cu²⁺)
rubric: In a flame test, Ca²⁺ gives a brick-red flame, Na⁺ gives yellow, K⁺ gives lilac/violet, and Cu²⁺ gives blue-green.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Acid rain is caused mainly by atmospheric
options: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides|Carbon dioxide|Ozone|Water vapour
rubric: Acid rain results from the dissolution of sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) — released from burning fossil fuels — in atmospheric water to form sulphuric and nitric acids.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The empirical formula of a compound shows
options: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms|The actual number of atoms|The structural arrangement|The number of isomers
answer: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms
rubric: The empirical formula shows the simplest integer ratio of atoms of each element in a compound — e.g., glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) has empirical formula CH₂O.
